title: Welcome to Singapore FinTech Festival 2026
description: Join us as we kick off SFF 2026 on the Festival Stage, featuring insightful conversations, groundbreaking ideas, and inspiring voices shaping the future of FinTech.
description_zh: 歡迎一同在 Festival Stage 為 SFF 2026 揭開序幕，透過富有洞見的對話、突破性的構想與啟發人心的聲音，共同塑造金融科技的未來。

title: AI and the Five Forces Rewiring Finance
description: AI is arriving as finance is being reshaped by geoeconomic fragmentation, technological change, shifting capital, talent constraints and evolving policy. Its effects will not be uniform: the same capabilities that widen access and improve productivity could also concentrate advantage, deepen dependencies and test the resilience of institutions and markets. Drawing on a global view of finance and public policy, this keynote examines where AI could accelerate these ruptures, where it might help bridge them, and what choices will determine the difference. The session asks what must be rewired for financial systems to remain trusted, inclusive and resilient.
description_zh: 在地緣經濟碎片化、技術變革、資本流向轉變、人才限制及政策演進重塑金融業之際，AI 正式登場。它帶來的影響不會一致：同樣能擴大服務可及性、提高生產力的能力，也可能使優勢更加集中、加深依賴，並考驗機構與市場的韌性。本場主題演講從金融與公共政策的全球視角出發，探討 AI 可能在哪些地方加劇這些斷裂、在哪些地方有助於彌合它們，以及哪些選擇將決定不同的結果。本場將探問，金融體系必須進行哪些重塑，才能持續值得信賴、具包容性且富有韌性。

title: From Digital to Intelligent: Who Will Build the Next Financial System?
description: Asia’s financial system is entering its next transformation. As AI, real-time payments and embedded finance reshape how money moves and financial services are delivered, the boundaries between banks, technology companies and platforms are rapidly dissolving. This session explores who will build, and control, the next generation of financial infrastructure. The conversation examines how technology and traditional finance will converge, where new sources of competitive advantage will emerge, and whether Asia will pioneer a fundamentally new model for intelligent, interconnected finance.
description_zh: 亞洲金融體系正邁入下一階段的轉型。隨著 AI、即時支付及嵌入式金融重塑資金流動與金融服務的提供方式，銀行、科技公司與平台之間的界線正迅速消融。本場探討誰將建構並掌控下一代金融基礎設施。對話將檢視科技與傳統金融如何融合、新的競爭優勢將從何處出現，以及亞洲是否將率先開創一種根本嶄新的智慧互聯金融模式。

title: Building the Capacity to Thrive: Can Digital Infrastructure Create the Next Generation of Inclusive Economies?
description: Digital infrastructure can lower barriers to financial services, markets and public support, but access alone does not guarantee participation or prosperity. The harder task is building the skills, institutions, trust and locally relevant services that let people and businesses turn connectivity into opportunity. Drawing on experience across policy, development and fintech, this session examines what helps digital systems reach underserved communities, support livelihoods and strengthen local economies, and where infrastructure-led strategies fall short. Attendees will leave with a clearer view of the capabilities required to make digital growth genuinely inclusive.
description_zh: 數位基礎設施能降低取得金融服務、進入市場及獲得公共支援的門檻，但僅有使用管道，並不保證能參與其中或享有繁榮。更艱鉅的任務，是建立技能、制度、信任與符合在地需求的服務，讓個人與企業將連結轉化為機會。本場汲取政策、發展及金融科技領域的經驗，探討哪些因素有助於數位系統觸及服務不足的社群、支持生計並強化地方經濟，以及以基礎設施為主導的策略在哪些地方力有未逮。與會者將更清楚了解，要讓數位成長真正具包容性，需要具備哪些能力。

title: The Future of Growth: Jobs, Skills and Productivity in an AI Economy
description:
The next phase of economic growth may depend on how successfully countries navigate a fundamental transition in the world of work.

AI and automation are changing the skills businesses need, the way jobs are organised and the potential for economies to become more productive. At the same time, many countries face a difficult paradox: businesses cannot find the skills they need, while millions of workers need new pathways into employment.

For governments, this is not simply a question of education or labour policy. It is a question of growth — how to raise productivity, create jobs, help businesses adopt new technologies and ensure that the gains from technological change translate into broader economic opportunity.

This ministerial panel will explore the choices facing governments as they prepare their economies for the next decade: Where should governments invest? How should businesses and education systems share responsibility for building new skills? And how can countries turn AI-driven productivity gains into more jobs, higher incomes and broader prosperity?
description_zh: 下一階段的經濟成長，可能取決於各國能否成功因應工作世界的根本轉變。AI 與自動化正在改變企業所需的技能、工作的組織方式，以及各經濟體提升生產力的潛力。同時，許多國家面臨一個棘手的矛盾：企業找不到所需技能，而數百萬名勞工卻需要新的就業途徑。對政府而言，這不只是教育或勞動政策的問題，更是成長的問題：如何提高生產力、創造就業、協助企業採用新技術，並確保技術變革帶來的收益能轉化為更廣泛的經濟機會。本場部長級座談將探討政府為未來十年經濟發展做準備時所面臨的選擇：政府應投資哪些領域？企業與教育體系應如何共同承擔培養新技能的責任？各國又該如何將 AI 帶來的生產力提升，轉化為更多就業機會、更高收入與更普遍的繁榮？

title: Pay It Forward
description: Whether you're a student starting out, a finance professional planning a career pivot, or a startup founder facing a specific business challenge, Pay It Forward connects you with established industry professionals for face-to-face, one-to-one mentorship. It's a chance to get advice from people who have already worked through the challenges you're facing. Sessions are 15 minutes long and take place at the Pay It Forward Lounge in Hall 3, from 18 to 20 November, 12.30pm to 4.30pm. Come with one specific question or challenge, and leave with focused, practical advice.
description_zh: 無論你是剛起步的學生、計畫轉換職涯方向的金融專業人士，還是面臨特定商業挑戰的新創公司創辦人，Pay It Forward 都能讓你與資深業界專業人士面對面，接受一對一的導師指導。你將有機會向曾經克服你目前所遇挑戰的人請益。每次交流為 15 分鐘，於 11 月 18 日至 20 日下午 12:30 至 4:30，在第 3 展廳的 Pay It Forward Lounge 舉行。帶著一個具體問題或挑戰前來，帶走聚焦且實用的建議。

title: Welcome to Policy Stage - Day 1
description: Join us as we kick off the day's sessions on the Policy Stage, featuring insightful conversations, groundbreaking ideas, and inspiring voices shaping the future of FinTech.
description_zh: 歡迎一同為 Policy Stage 當天的議程揭開序幕，透過富有洞見的對話、突破性的構想與啟發人心的聲音，共同塑造金融科技的未來。

title: Building Human Experiences with AI
Central Banks and Future Payment Systems: Priorities, Trade-offs, and Opportunities for Cross-Border Collaboration
speakers: Anna Nordstrom; Daranee Saeju; Tommaso Mancini-Griffoli
description: As financial systems evolve, central banks face a dual challenge -modernising the infrastructure that works today while building the foundations for what comes next. This means making strategic choices around the future of digital money and settlement, wholesale and retail systems connectivity across borders, and the interoperability, liquidity and governance arrangements that underpin them. At the same time, an increasingly AI-enabled financial system is raising the bar for the safety, reliability and resilience of critical payment infrastructure. This panel will discuss the key building blocks for the next generation of payments and where deeper cross-border collaboration can deliver capabilities that individual jurisdictions cannot achieve alone.
description_zh: 隨著金融體系演進，中央銀行面臨雙重挑戰：既要將現行運作的基礎設施現代化，也要為未來奠定基礎。這意味著必須針對數位貨幣與結算的未來、批發及零售系統的跨境連結，以及支撐這些系統的互通性、流動性與治理安排，做出策略選擇。同時，日益由 AI 賦能的金融體系，也提高了關鍵支付基礎設施在安全性、可靠性與韌性方面的要求。本場座談將討論下一代支付的關鍵構成要素，以及哪些領域能透過更深入的跨境合作，建立單一司法管轄區無法獨力實現的能力。

title: Rewiring the Founder Playbook: Welcome to Founders Stage - Day 1
description:
Hard Decisions behind Companies that Last.

Capital. Customers. Control. Growth. Exit.The rules have changed. What must a company get right to keep building in 2027?

The founder playbook is being rewired. Capital comes with harder terms. Enterprise buyers can build, wait or buy. AI can make a product look brilliant - and make it easier to copy. Growth no longer guarantees a path to liquidity.

Rewiring the Founder Playbook brings founders, investors, enterprise leaders and policymakers together for the conversations that usually happen behind closed doors: how to protect equity when financing gets hard; what evidence earns a term sheet; whether a customer will share risk; what makes a moat real; and when an acqui-hire or asset sale is the smartest decision a founder can make.

Across the three days, the Founders Stage will be anchored by flagship Founders Peak talks - the personal stories behind the pivotal decisions - alongside candid, future-facing practitioner conversations on the capital, customer, policy and exit choices that will determine who is still standing in 2027.

These are not retrospective success stories or generic startup panels. Each session asks one question: what must be true in 2027 for this company to earn the right to keep building?
description_zh: 長青企業背後的艱難抉擇。資本。客戶。控制權。成長。退場。規則已經改變。企業必須在哪些方面做對，才能在 2027 年持續建設與發展？創辦人的經營指南正在被重塑。資金附帶的條件更加嚴苛。企業買家可以自行開發、等待，或購買。AI 能讓產品看起來出色，也能讓它更容易被複製。成長不再保證能找到變現途徑。「Rewiring the Founder Playbook」匯聚創辦人、投資人、企業領袖與政策制定者，展開通常只在閉門場合進行的對話：融資艱難時如何保護股權；哪些證據能換來投資條款書；客戶是否願意分擔風險；什麼能形成真正的護城河；以及何時以收購取得人才或出售資產，會是創辦人最明智的決定。在三天活動中，Founders Stage 將以旗艦 Founders Peak 演講為主軸，分享關鍵決策背後的親身故事，同時搭配坦誠且面向未來的實務工作者對話，討論將決定誰能在 2027 年繼續屹立不搖的資本、客戶、政策及退場選擇。這些並非回顧式的成功故事，也不是泛泛而談的新創座談。每場議程都追問同一個問題：到了 2027 年，這家公司必須具備哪些條件，才有資格繼續建設與發展？

title: Welcome to Catalyst Stage - Day 1
description: Join us as we kick off the day's sessions on the Catalyst Stage, featuring insightful conversations, groundbreaking ideas, and inspiring voices shaping the next wave of talent and ideas.
description_zh: 歡迎一同為 Catalyst Stage 當天的議程揭開序幕，透過富有洞見的對話、突破性的構想與啟發人心的聲音，共同孕育下一波人才與創意。

title: Welcome to FutureMatters Stage - Day 1
description: Join us as we kick off the day's sessions on the FutureMatters Stage, featuring insightful conversations, groundbreaking ideas, and inspiring voices shaping the future of FinTech.
description_zh: 歡迎一同為 FutureMatters Stage 當天的議程揭開序幕，透過富有洞見的對話、突破性的構想與啟發人心的聲音，共同塑造金融科技的未來。

title: The $43 Billion Bet: Where Will Agentic AI Create Value in Finance?
description:
Agentic AI is moving rapidly from concept to deployment, but its trajectory across financial services is far from uniform. Institutions are experimenting with autonomous agents across markets, functions and business models, while adoption, ambition and readiness vary significantly.

This opening conversation takes stock of the emerging global landscape: where is agentic AI gaining real traction, which parts of finance are moving fastest, and what are institutions learning as they move from experimentation towards deployment? Most importantly, as the technology develops at different speeds and in different ways, where could the next wave of value emerge?
description_zh: 代理型 AI 正迅速從概念走向部署，但在金融服務領域的發展軌跡遠非一致。各機構正在不同市場、職能與商業模式中試驗自主代理，而採用程度、企圖心及準備程度卻有顯著差異。本場開場對話將盤點正在成形的全球局勢：代理型 AI 在哪些領域真正獲得進展？金融業哪些部分的步伐最快？機構從試驗走向部署的過程中，又學到了什麼？最重要的是，當這項技術以不同速度及方式發展時，下一波價值可能從何處湧現？

title: Is Southeast Asia's Capital Winter Structural, Or Cyclical?
description: While early-stage seed activity persists, growth capital across Southeast Asia remains intensely concentrated and selective. PitchBook's 2026 Southeast Asia Private Capital Breakdown recorded VC deal value falling 33.9% in 2025, driven by tighter diligence and reduced cross-border participation. Investors holding dry powder are enforcing higher performance hurdles and stricter profitability milestones before committing follow-on capital. This session addresses how regional GPs are deploying funds, what alternative capital stacks are stepping into the void, and where funding will genuinely flow.
description_zh: 雖然早期種子輪投資活動持續，東南亞的成長資本仍高度集中，且篩選極為嚴格。PitchBook 的《2026 年東南亞私募資本分析》記錄顯示，由於盡職調查趨嚴及跨境參與減少，2025 年創投交易金額下降了 33.9%。手握待投資金的投資人，在承諾後續投資前，正要求更高的績效門檻與更嚴格的獲利里程碑。本場探討區域內的普通合夥人（GP）如何部署資金、哪些替代資本組合正在填補缺口，以及資金究竟會流向何處。

title: The Trust Crisis of Agentic Commerce: Why AI Will Force Us to Reinvent Financial Security - Powered by Visa
description: As AI reshapes commerce, it is also reshaping financial crime. Deepfakes, synthetic identities and organised fraud networks are enabling attacks at unprecedented scale and speed. This session explores how security must shift from authenticating transactions to authenticating actors, human or machine. It also looks at why the organisations that thrive will be those that build the intelligence, visibility and response infrastructure needed to protect trust in an increasingly automated economy.
description_zh: AI 在重塑商業的同時，也在重塑金融犯罪。深度偽造、合成身分與有組織的詐欺網絡，使攻擊得以以前所未有的規模與速度進行。本場探討安全防護為何必須從驗證交易，轉向驗證行為主體，無論是人類或機器。也將探討，為何在日益自動化的經濟中，能蓬勃發展的組織，將是那些建立所需情報、可視性與應變基礎設施以守護信任的組織。

title: Stablecoins at Speed: Real-Time Visibility and Control for BIN Sponsors - Powered by Thredd
description: Stablecoin-enabled card programmes move at real-time speed, creating oversight challenges that traditional monitoring can't match. This joint session brings together a market view of the risks emerging in stablecoin card programmes and a technology view of how to manage them. It shows how card processors can give BIN sponsors real-time visibility and control at scale.
description_zh: 採用穩定幣的卡片計畫以即時速度運作，帶來傳統監控方式難以應付的監督挑戰。本場聯合議程結合市場與技術兩種視角，前者檢視穩定幣卡片計畫中正在浮現的風險，後者探討如何管理這些風險，並展示卡片處理服務商如何大規模地為 BIN 贊助機構提供即時可視性與控制能力。

title: How Can Agentic AI Create a Commercial and Competitive Advantage?
speakers: Himal Makwana; Melvyn Low; Derrick Goh; Pat Patel
description:
As AI capabilities become more widely available, financial institutions face a harder question: what will make their use of the technology difficult to replicate? Access to models alone offers little assurance of lasting differentiation.

Where can agentic AI generate additional revenue, improve pricing or make previously uneconomical services viable? Does advantage come from proprietary data, distribution, partnerships or the ability to redesign a business proposition?

This conversation examines which strategic choices could create defensible value, and what evidence would justify committing capital to them.
description_zh: 隨著 AI 能力日益普及，金融機構面臨一個更棘手的問題：什麼能讓它們運用這項技術的方式難以被複製？僅僅取得模型，幾乎無法保證持久的差異化優勢。代理型 AI 能在哪些領域創造額外營收、改善定價，或讓過去不具經濟效益的服務變得可行？優勢來自專有資料、通路、合作關係，還是重新設計商業價值主張的能力？本場對話探討哪些策略選擇能創造可守護的價值，以及哪些證據足以支持投入資金。

title: The Agentic Enterprise: When Intelligence Executes Intent in Commerce - Powered by Visa
description: AI is changing how businesses buy, pay and move money. Systems can now interpret intent and orchestrate invoice approval, payment execution and reconciliation as a single journey within defined controls. This shift is not about faster payments. It is a move from managing transactions to managing outcomes. Hear practical examples, a framework for the agentic enterprise, and what it takes in trust and infrastructure to scale agentic commerce responsibly.
description_zh: AI 正在改變企業採購、付款與調動資金的方式。系統如今能理解意圖，並在既定的控制措施內，將發票核准、支付執行與對帳串連成單一流程。這項轉變不在於更快的支付，而在於從管理交易轉向管理成果。本場將分享實際案例、代理型企業的架構，以及負責任地擴大代理型商務規模，在信任與基礎設施方面需要具備的條件。

title: The New Rails into China: Cards, Wallets, QR and Remittance - Powered by Tencent
description: As international visitors return to China in growing numbers, the way money flows into the country is being rebuilt across several rails at once: international cards linked to domestic mobile wallets, overseas e-wallets connecting directly to local acceptance networks, cross-border QR interoperability, and next-generation remittance channels. What does it take to connect these rails, and what opportunities does it open up for payment providers, banks, merchants and fintechs worldwide?
description_zh: 隨著重返中國的國際旅客日益增加，資金流入中國的方式正同時透過多種管道重建：國際卡片連結境內行動錢包、境外電子錢包直接接入本地受理網絡、跨境 QR 碼互通，以及新一代匯款管道。連結這些管道需要哪些條件？這又將為全球支付服務商、銀行、商家與金融科技公司開啟哪些機會？

title: MUFG Young Innovators Showcase
description:
Nine MUFG Young Innovators from Odisha step onto a global stage.

Made possible through MUFG's support, this session brings students from India's emerging FinTech ecosystem, who have undergone the Certificate in FinTech and InsurTech programme, before an international audience of industry leaders, investors and policymakers. The session features a live showcase from the cohort's winning team, presenting the work that earned them their place here.

A demonstration of what happens when talent is met with opportunity and a look at where the next generation of financial innovation is coming from.
description_zh: 來自印度奧迪沙邦的九位 MUFG Young Innovators 將登上全球舞台。在 MUFG 的支持下，本場讓來自印度新興金融科技生態系、已完成金融科技與保險科技證書課程的學生，站到由業界領袖、投資人及政策制定者組成的國際觀眾面前。本場將由該梯次的獲勝團隊進行現場展示，呈現使他們獲得此次舞台機會的作品。這既展示人才遇上機會時會發生什麼，也讓我們看見下一代金融創新正從何處誕生。

title: From Intelligence to Auditable Action: What It Takes to Run AI Agents in Financial Services - Powered by Tencent
description: Financial institutions aren’t short of intelligence. They are short of agents they will let act. Running AI agents in regulated finance requires bounded permissions, traceable actions and defensible outcomes. The challenge is no longer just what AI can do, but how institutions can govern what it does and prove it.
description_zh: 金融機構並不缺乏智慧，缺的是它們願意授權採取行動的代理。在受監管的金融領域運行 AI 代理，需要明確界定的權限、可追溯的行動，以及經得起檢驗的結果。挑戰不再只是 AI 能做什麼，而是機構如何治理 AI 所做的事，並提出證明。

title: Stablecoins: From Fringe to Framework
speakers: Nicole Sandler; Peter Kerstens; Walter Hessert; Gabriel Lee
description: Stablecoins have moved out of the regulatory grey zone and into a proper legal framework. That shift changes the question facing every institution, from whether to engage at all to exactly how. Regulators in different markets are setting the terms at different speeds, and institutions no longer have the luxury of waiting for global consensus before deciding. This discussion works through the practical choices on the table: issuing, distributing or custodying stablecoins directly, against the risk of simply watching deposits drift toward whichever option moves fastest. Participants leave with a sharper sense of where their own institution sits on that spectrum, and what waiting actually costs under the new rules. One key question the discussion will dive into: whether to issue, distribute or custody stablecoins themselves, or simply watch deposits migrate to them regardless.
description_zh: 穩定幣已經走出監理灰色地帶，進入正式的法律框架。這個轉變改變了每一家機構要面對的問題——從「要不要參與」變成「究竟要怎麼參與」。各市場的監理機關訂定規則的速度不一，機構已經沒有餘裕等全球共識形成後再決定。本場討論梳理檯面上的實際選項：自行發行、負責分銷或直接提供託管，對照「眼睜睜看著存款流向動作最快的那一方」的風險。與會者將更清楚自家機構落在這個光譜的哪個位置，以及在新規則之下，等待的實際代價是什麼。討論將深入的一個關鍵問題：該自己發行、分銷或託管穩定幣，還是無論如何都只能看著存款遷移過去？

title: Built for Chaos: How Asia's Fintechs are Rewriting Global Payments - Powered by Banking Circle
description: While Western payment giants race to crack Asia's fragmented markets, the region's homegrown fintechs have quietly gone the other way, expanding into Europe and the US. A moderated conversation with two cross-border payments leaders explores what mastering Asia's complexity has taught them about winning on the global stage.
description_zh: 當西方支付巨擘競相攻克亞洲分散的市場時，該區域的本土金融科技公司卻悄悄朝相反方向前進，擴展至歐洲與美國。本場由主持人引導兩位跨境支付領袖對話，探討掌握亞洲的複雜性，讓他們學到了哪些在全球舞台取勝的經驗。

title: How Can Agentic AI Create Cost And Operational Advantages?
speakers: Alvaro Garrido; Giorgio Migliarina; Kfir Godrich; Patrick Chan; Ned Lowe
description:
An agent that completes a task faster does not necessarily make an operation cheaper. Integration, supervision, exceptions and maintenance can absorb the savings promised by automation.

Which workflows offer a credible return once the full cost of deployment is included? How should institutions redesign processes, allocate work between people and agents, and measure improvements in throughput, accuracy and service quality?

This conversation focuses on the economics of running agentic operations, including when greater autonomy delivers value and when a simpler approach remains more effective. How organisations redesigning operating models using this technology?
description_zh: 代理更快完成任務，不一定能降低營運成本。整合、監督、例外處理與維護，可能抵銷自動化承諾帶來的節省。將部署的全部成本納入計算後，哪些工作流程仍能帶來可信的回報？機構應如何重新設計流程、在人員與代理之間分配工作，並衡量處理量、準確性與服務品質的改善？本場對話聚焦代理型營運的經濟效益，包括何時更高的自主性可以創造價值，以及何時較簡單的方法仍然更有效。組織正如何運用這項技術重新設計營運模式？

title: Global Fintech Hackcelerator
RWA & Tokenization: When the Asset Becomes a Token, What Happens to the Rules?
description:
Tokenisation is moving real-world assets such as treasuries, funds and credit onto new digital rails. The technology is advancing quickly. The harder question is whether the legal and regulatory framework can keep pace.

When an asset becomes a token, does it retain the same rights and protections? Who owns the underlying asset? Which jurisdiction's rules apply when the token crosses a border? And what happens when different markets take different approaches?

This conversation brings regulators and market participants together to examine where the rules are clear, where they diverge, and what still needs to be resolved for tokenised assets to scale.
description_zh: 代幣化正將國債、基金及信貸等現實世界資產移轉至新的數位軌道。技術進展迅速，更艱鉅的問題則是法律與監管架構能否跟上。當一項資產成為代幣，它是否保有相同的權利與保障？誰擁有底層資產？代幣跨境時，適用哪個司法管轄區的規則？不同市場採取不同做法時，又會發生什麼？本場對話匯聚監管機關與市場參與者，檢視哪些規則已經明確、哪些出現分歧，以及代幣化資產要擴大規模，還有哪些問題必須解決。

title: Will Enterprise Buyers Build or Buy External Software in 2027?
description: Enterprise software procurement has reached an impasse where buyers are actively delaying third-party purchasing decisions. McKinsey's State of AI Survey reveals that while corporate adoption has expanded to 72% of organizations, less than a third have realized material bottom-line cost reductions, driving IT leaders to build custom internal workflows or freeze deployments. With internal developer efficiency rising, buying commercial software requires clear justification. This session brings enterprise procurement chiefs and CIOs together to uncover the cost benchmarks, integration constraints, and security liabilities that determine whether they buy, build internally, or wait.
description_zh: 企業軟體採購已陷入僵局，買家正主動延後第三方採購決策。麥肯錫的《AI 現況調查》顯示，雖然企業採用率已擴大至 72%，但實現顯著成本下降、對獲利產生實質影響的企業不到三分之一，促使資訊科技主管自行建立客製化內部工作流程，或凍結部署。隨著內部開發人員效率提高，購買商用軟體需要明確的理由。本場匯聚企業採購主管與資訊長，揭示決定他們購買、內部自行開發或等待的成本基準、整合限制及安全責任。

title: Can Regulation Be Written Into Money Itself? The Case for Rules in the Rails, Tokenized Deposits & Conditional Money
speakers: Dr. Eva Hüpkes; Kazuki Ueda; Vira Platonova
description: Tokenised deposits and conditional money take the programmability idea one layer deeper. They pilot whether settlement, eligibility and compliance can be embedded directly in the money rather than enforced around it. That raises a regulatory question few frameworks have caught up with: who is liable when the rule embedded in the transaction, not a human decision, turns out to be wrong. This discussion examines how the embedded-rules approach works in practice, and what it removes from the compliance function. It also looks at what new failure modes this introduces once the rule is baked into the transfer rather than checked afterwards. Attendees leave with a clearer view of where this model is genuinely ready, and where regulators are still working out how to hold it accountable. One key question the discussion will dive into: if compliance is embedded in the money itself, who is accountable when the embedded rule is wrong?
description_zh: 代幣化存款與條件式貨幣，將可程式化的概念再推進一層。它們試驗能否將結算、資格條件與法規遵循直接嵌入貨幣，而不是在貨幣周邊加以執行。這引出了一個鮮少有現行架構能處理的監管問題：當出錯的是嵌入交易中的規則，而非人為決策時，誰應承擔責任？本場討論將檢視嵌入規則的方法如何在實務中運作，以及它能減少哪些法遵職能工作。也將探討，當規則直接內建於轉帳，而非事後檢查時，會引入哪些新的失效模式。與會者將更清楚了解，這種模式在哪些方面已真正準備就緒，以及監管機關在哪些方面仍在摸索如何確保問責。討論將深入探究的一個關鍵問題是：若法規遵循被嵌入貨幣本身，當內建規則出錯時，誰應負責？

title: Identity Infrastructure: The Missing Layer in an AI-Powered Financial System - Powered by Kybix
description: Permissioned identity is emerging as critical infrastructure for trusted client relationships in an AI-powered financial ecosystem. This fireside chat explores how building this foundation can enable AI adoption at scale, deliver smarter client experiences, and strengthen risk controls. We’ll also discuss how established institutions and emerging ecosystem players can work together to build sustainable, trusted foundations for long-term success.
description_zh: 在 AI 驅動的金融生態系中，授權式身分正成為建立可信客戶關係的關鍵基礎設施。本場爐邊對談探討，建立這項基礎如何促成大規模採用 AI、提供更智慧的客戶體驗，並強化風險控制。我們也將討論，既有機構與新興生態系參與者如何攜手，為長期成功建立永續且值得信賴的基礎。

title: What Are The Unintended Consequences of Scaling Agentic AI?
speakers: Lito Villanueva; Prof. Amanda Brock; Virginie Barbot
description: AI agents will not only serve customers and execute payments. They will also be used to impersonate customers, automate fraud and probe financial infrastructure at unprecedented speed. Traditional controls built around human behaviour and manual intervention may no longer respond fast enough. This session examines how financial institutions can deploy autonomous defence, distinguish legitimate agents from malicious ones and contain threats without blocking genuine transactions.
description_zh: AI 代理不僅會服務客戶與執行支付，也會被用來冒充客戶、自動化詐欺，並以前所未有的速度探測金融基礎設施。圍繞人類行為與人工介入所建立的傳統控制措施，可能已無法及時應對。本場探討金融機構如何部署自主防禦、區分合法與惡意代理，以及在不阻擋真實交易的情況下遏制威脅。

title: How Will Agentic AI Change the Customer Touchpoint?
speakers: Daniel Hong; Lee Zhu Kuang; Shayan Hazir; T.R. Ramachandran; Nishtha Asthana
description:
Digital banking has largely been designed around customers visiting an app, comparing options and making a choice. If customers delegate those choices to agents, banks may have fewer direct opportunities to earn their attention and trust.

How will customers discover, select and remain loyal to financial providers when software mediates the relationship? Which interactions will people still want to handle themselves? This session examines how channels, service design and customer consent must evolve, and what institutions need to preserve a meaningful relationship with the person behind the agent.
description_zh: 數位銀行服務的設計，大多建立在客戶開啟應用程式、比較選項並做出選擇的模式上。若客戶將這些選擇交由代理處理，銀行可能就更少有機會直接贏得他們的關注與信任。當軟體居中協調關係時，客戶將如何發現、選擇金融服務提供者，並保持忠誠？哪些互動仍是人們希望親自處理的？本場檢視通路、服務設計與客戶同意機制必須如何演進，以及機構需要具備哪些條件，才能與代理背後的那個人維持有意義的關係。

title: Presence is the Product: Redefining the Financial Advisor of the Future - Powered by Accenture
description: Advice has always been sold on presence: the advisor who knows you and is there when it matters. Technology scaled transactions, not presence. Agentic AI changes that. An advisor backed by AI agents can continuously serve hundreds of clients. This session demonstrates agentic AI in wealth management beyond CRM and lead generation, empowering advisors holistically, and explores what it takes to deploy it in production.
description_zh: 顧問服務向來以陪伴為賣點：顧問了解你，並在重要時刻在你身邊。科技擴大了交易規模，卻未擴大陪伴的規模。代理型 AI 改變了這一點。獲得 AI 代理支援的顧問，可以持續服務數百名客戶。本場展示代理型 AI 在財富管理中的應用，超越客戶關係管理（CRM）與潛在客戶開發，全面賦能顧問，並探討將其部署至正式營運環境所需的條件。

title: Making Agentic Payments Mainstream: The Money Stack - Powered by Tazapay
description: Agentic payments need more than smarter models to go mainstream. They need a new money stack of real-time settlement rails, agent-level policy controls and governance that earns trust at scale. What will it take to move from pilots to everyday commerce?
description_zh: 代理型支付若要成為主流，光靠更智慧的模型並不足夠。它需要一套新的貨幣技術架構，包含即時結算軌道、代理層級的政策控制，以及能在大規模應用下贏得信任的治理。從試點走向日常商業活動，需要具備哪些條件？

title: The Agentic Era: How AI is Rewriting the Future of Financial Services - Powered by AWS
description: Financial services is entering a new phase where AI systems don't just assist, they act, orchestrating decisions across compliance, fraud detection, and customer engagement in real time. This session examines how the convergence of agentic AI with tokenization, stablecoins, and agentic commerce is reshaping payments infrastructure and core banking, and what FSI leaders need to consider as they move from generative AI pilots to autonomous systems operating at scale.
description_zh: 金融服務正進入一個新階段，AI 系統不再只是協助，而是採取行動，即時統籌法規遵循、詐欺偵測與客戶互動各方面的決策。本場檢視代理型 AI 與代幣化、穩定幣及代理型商務的融合，如何重塑支付基礎設施與核心銀行業務，以及金融服務業領導者從生成式 AI 試點走向大規模運作的自主系統時，需要考量哪些事項。

title: Cross-Border Connectivity: How Regional Blocs are Building Their Own Financial Integration
speakers: Clara B. Arthur; José Beltrán; Yasuto Watanabe; Maha El Dimachki
description:
Not every country can build global-scale financial infrastructure alone. Across the world, groups of countries are pooling resources, coordinating oversight, and interlinking systems regionally, choosing collective action over waiting for a single global standard or going it alone.

This panel brings together three different models of that regional playbook. The discussion works through what it takes to build financial cooperation at the bloc level: how these regional mechanisms actually got built, what kept smaller or newer members willing to join in, and where this collective model succeeds — or strains — compared to a single institution building alone. Attendees leave with a practical view of when banding together beats going it alone, and what it costs to make that work.
description_zh: 並非每個國家都能獨力建構全球規模的金融基礎設施。在世界各地，多國集團正匯集資源、協調監督，並在區域內互連系統，選擇集體行動，而非等待單一全球標準或各自為政。本場座談匯聚這種區域合作策略的三種不同模式。討論將逐步檢視在區域集團層級建立金融合作所需的條件：這些區域機制究竟如何建成、什麼讓較小或較新的成員願意加入，以及相較於單一機構獨力建構，這種集體模式在哪些地方取得成功，又在哪些地方承受壓力。與會者將從實務角度了解，何時攜手合作勝過單打獨鬥，以及讓合作發揮作用需要付出什麼代價。

title: What Will the Strongest and Weakest Moats Look Like in 2027?
description: Rapid advances in foundation models and automated engineering have flattened traditional competitive moats. McKinsey's 2026 State of AI report found nearly a third of enterprises now choose to build functionality in-house with AI agents rather than buy it, the clearest signal that a product-level moat alone no longer holds. Defensibility is consolidating around regulatory licenses, proprietary data integrations, and entrenched distribution. This session challenges investors to evaluate the structural integrity of modern technology moats: which advantages endure, and which are eroding under platform pressure. Source: McKinsey & Company, The State of AI 2026.
description_zh: 基礎模型與自動化工程的快速進步，已削弱傳統競爭護城河。麥肯錫《2026 年 AI 現況報告》發現，如今近三分之一的企業選擇利用 AI 代理在內部開發功能，而非採購；這是最明確的訊號，顯示僅有產品層級的護城河已不足以維持優勢。防禦能力正集中於監管牌照、專有資料整合及根深柢固的通路。本場將促使投資人檢驗現代科技護城河的結構穩固性：哪些優勢能持續，哪些則正在平台壓力下被侵蝕。來源：McKinsey & Company，《The State of AI 2026》。

title: Quantum-Safe Readiness: How Do You Really Measure Up? - Powered by ST Engineering
description: Financial institutions have begun crypto screening, built inventories, and launched pilots. The next question is how their progress compares with the market—and whether it is sufficient for the risks they face. Drawing on published banking-sector readiness data, this session explores how to benchmark progress, interpret peer comparisons, and assess the evidence behind readiness claims. From inventory coverage to migration capability and supplier dependencies, it examines why being ahead of the market can still leave critical gaps. Participants will gain practical questions to assess where they stand and prioritise their next steps.
description_zh: 金融機構已開始進行密碼技術篩查、建立資產清冊並啟動試點。下一個問題是，它們的進展與市場相比如何，以及是否足以因應所面臨的風險。本場依據已發布的銀行業準備程度資料，探討如何設定進度基準、解讀同業比較，以及評估準備就緒聲明背後的證據。從清冊涵蓋範圍、遷移能力到供應商依賴，將檢視為何即使領先市場，仍可能存在關鍵缺口。與會者將獲得實用的檢視問題，以評估自身所處位置，並為下一步行動排定優先順序。

title: When Agentic AI Meets Programmable Money, What Comes Next?
speakers: Evy Theunis; Kash Razzaghi; Sanjay Saraf; Sunayna Tuteja
description: Three forces are colliding at once—autonomous agents, programmable stablecoins, and real-time rails—and together they could rewrite how money moves entirely. As AI agents begin to transact independently and stablecoins gain regulatory footing, the boundaries between payments, settlement, and currency are dissolving faster than most institutions can react. Learn how agentic payments and stablecoins intersect to enable machine-speed money movement; what infrastructure and compliance shifts this convergence demands; and where the earliest commercial opportunities are emerging.
description_zh: 三股力量正同時交會：自主代理、可程式化穩定幣，以及即時支付軌道，它們結合後可能徹底改寫資金流動的方式。隨著 AI 代理開始獨立交易，穩定幣逐步取得監管上的立足點，支付、結算與貨幣之間的界線，正以超出多數機構反應能力的速度消融。本場將說明代理型支付與穩定幣如何交會，實現機器速度的資金流動；這項融合需要哪些基礎設施與法遵方面的轉變；以及最早的商業機會正在哪裡浮現。

title: Who Builds the Bridge Between National Payment Schemes; and Who Owns the Toll?
speakers: Alan Ni; Lawrence Chan; Jo Yeo
description:
National instant payment schemes are proliferating around the world, yet most remain valuable only within their own borders. As domestic networks mature, the next source of value lies not in individual schemes, but in the bridges that connect them.

This session explores the emerging cross-border interoperability layer: who is building it, how common messaging standards and technical frameworks make it possible, and how governance, costs, revenues, and risks are shared among the parties involved. The discussion will examine the different models being adopted globally, from bilateral connections to multilateral networks and shared infrastructure platforms.

Participants will leave with a clearer understanding of where payment interoperability is succeeding in practice, what challenges remain, and the trade-offs between different connectivity approaches.

One of the central questions the panel will explore is: when one country's instant payment scheme needs to communicate with another's, who builds the bridge, and who owns the toll?
description_zh: 國家級即時支付計畫正在全球各地蓬勃發展，但多數仍只在本國境內具有價值。隨著國內網絡成熟，下一個價值來源不在個別計畫本身，而在連結它們的橋梁。本場探討正在成形的跨境互通層：誰正在建構它、共同訊息標準與技術架構如何使其成為可能，以及參與各方如何分配治理、成本、收益與風險。討論將檢視全球正在採用的不同模式，從雙邊連結、多邊網絡，到共用基礎設施平台。與會者將更清楚了解，支付互通性在哪些地方已取得實際成功、仍有哪些挑戰，以及不同連結方式之間的取捨。本場座談將探討的一個核心問題是：當一國的即時支付計畫需要與另一國互通時，誰來架橋，通行費又歸誰所有？

title: Inclusive Instant Payments: Building a Commercially Sustainable National Roadmap
speakers: Jean Bosco Iyacu; Kosta Peric; Sateesh Palagiri; Sara Brites; Pat Patel
description:
Instant payments can reach millions of the unbanked—but only if the economics work for everyone building the rails. Around the world, national real-time payment systems are proving that speed and inclusion can coexist, yet many struggle to balance universal access with commercial viability. Getting that balance right is now a defining test of payments strategy.

You will learn: how to design instant payment schemes that serve the underserved without eroding sustainability; which governance and pricing models drive long-term adoption; and what lessons successful national roadmaps offer to markets still building theirs. Miss this session, and you risk designing a system that scales in usage but never in value.
description_zh: 即時支付能觸及數百萬名未獲銀行服務的人，但前提是對所有建設支付軌道的參與者而言，經濟上都可行。在全球各地，國家級即時支付系統證明速度與包容性可以並存，但許多系統仍難以在普及使用與商業可行性之間取得平衡。能否取得正確平衡，如今已成為支付策略的關鍵考驗。你將了解：如何設計服務不足群體也能使用、且不損及永續性的即時支付計畫；哪些治理與定價模式能推動長期採用；以及成功的國家發展藍圖，能為仍在建設中的市場提供哪些經驗。錯過本場，你可能設計出一套使用規模持續增加，價值卻始終無法隨之成長的系統。

title: Cross-Border Wholesale Connectivity: Building a More Connected Financial System
description:
As digital money, tokenised assets and next-generation financial infrastructures gain traction around the world, jurisdictions and institutions are adopting a growing range of technologies, infrastructure models and settlement systems. While this diversity is driving innovation, it also raises an important question: how can increasingly interconnected financial systems continue to operate seamlessly across borders — without waiting for a single global standard to emerge first?

This panel brings together the institutions alongside policymakers and innovators from Asia, Europe and the UK to discuss what regional cooperation actually requires in practice: unified ledgers, synchronisation mechanisms, privacy-preserving technologies, and the governance arrangements that let independently built systems trust one another.

The discussion will examine the technical, legal, operational and regulatory challenges involved in scaling these regional models, and explore how deeper connectivity between them — rather than a single unified global system — may be the more realistic path to an interconnected financial system.
description_zh: 隨著數位貨幣、代幣化資產與下一代金融基礎設施在世界各地逐漸普及，各司法管轄區與機構正採用愈來愈多樣的技術、基礎設施模式及結算系統。這種多樣性推動創新的同時，也提出一個重要問題：日益互聯的金融體系，如何在不必先等待單一全球標準出現的情況下，持續跨境無縫運作？本場座談匯聚相關機構，以及來自亞洲、歐洲與英國的政策制定者和創新者，討論區域合作在實務上究竟需要什麼：統一帳本、同步機制、隱私保護技術，以及讓各自獨立建構的系統能互相信任的治理安排。討論將檢視擴大這些區域模式所涉及的技術、法律、營運與監管挑戰，並探討深化彼此連結，而非建立單一統一的全球系統，為何可能是邁向互聯金融體系更務實的道路。

title: Is Cross-Border Mutual Recognition Through Sandboxes Now Closer or Farther?
description: Expanding across fragmented regional markets forces digital finance startups into repetitive licensing cycles that multiply compliance costs and stall international scale. Recent progress by Kenya and Rwanda’s central banks in establishing mutual licence-passporting demonstrates that cross-border supervisory reciprocity is workable in practice. A recent survey by TechCabal Research revealed that 62.5% of regional fintechs already operate internationally or plan to, with an identical proportion backing passporting frameworks. This session convenes financial regulators and founders to examine how central banks can align supervisory frameworks and establish mutual recognition standards without compromising financial stability or compliance oversight.
description_zh: 跨越分散的區域市場擴張，迫使數位金融新創公司反覆經歷申請牌照的流程，造成法遵成本倍增，並拖慢國際化發展。肯亞與盧安達中央銀行近期在建立牌照相互通行機制方面的進展，證明跨境監管互惠在實務上可行。TechCabal Research 最近的一項調查顯示，62.5% 的區域金融科技公司已在國際市場營運或計畫如此，同樣比例的公司支持牌照通行架構。本場匯聚金融監管機關與創辦人，探討中央銀行如何在不犧牲金融穩定與法遵監督的前提下，協調監管架構並建立相互承認標準。

title: Beyond the QR Code: What Moves China's Money Next? [Conducted in Mandarin]
description: China built the world's most pervasive mobile payments system on a black-and-white square. But when nearly every transaction runs through a QR code, where does the next leap come from? With the e-CNY pushing into wallets and cross-border rails like mBridge testing new models for settling value between central banks, the architecture of Chinese money is being redrawn. The panel unpacks which layers (digital currency, embedded finance, AI-driven credit or cross-border settlement) will capture the next wave of value. It also looks at what interoperability means for incumbents and foreign players, and how China's choices could set the template for payments across Asia.
description_zh: 中國憑藉一個黑白方格，建立了全球最普及的行動支付系統。但當幾乎每筆交易都透過 QR 碼完成，下一次躍進將從何而來？隨著數位人民幣（e-CNY）進入錢包，以及 mBridge 等跨境軌道試驗中央銀行之間價值結算的新模式，中國的貨幣架構正被重新描繪。本場座談將解析哪些層面，包括數位貨幣、嵌入式金融、AI 驅動的信貸或跨境結算，將掌握下一波價值。也將探討互通性對既有業者與外國參與者的意義，以及中國的選擇如何可能成為亞洲各地支付發展的範本。

title: The Founders ROCK
description: You don't want to miss this one-of-a-kind industry networking where founders, regulators, and business leaders will jam together on stage to wrap up and celebrate this milestone SFF with a BANG!
description_zh: 這場獨一無二的業界交流活動不容錯過！創辦人、監管者與企業領袖將同台即興演奏，以熱鬧震撼的方式，為這一屆具有里程碑意義的 SFF 收尾並一同慶祝！

Flash your SFF speaker pass to enjoy complimentary drinks and exclusive discounts at bars and restaurants along Clarke Quay, by the Singapore River — a networking experience you don't want to miss!

title: Welcome to Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 - Day 2
description: Join us as we kick off the day's sessions on the Festival Stage, featuring insightful conversations, groundbreaking ideas, and inspiring voices shaping the future of FinTech.
description_zh: 歡迎一同為 Festival Stage 當天的議程揭開序幕，透過富有洞見的對話、突破性的構想與啟發人心的聲音，共同塑造金融科技的未來。

title: Banking 5.0
description: Smart economies are beginning to make decisions and act across transport, energy, commerce and finance. Banking’s next shift may follow: AI agents could move from advising customers to initiating transactions, coordinating services and managing financial outcomes on their behalf. That prospect raises a structural question: can systems built around human instructions, batch payments and familiar forms of accountability support finance conducted at machine speed? The answer depends on more than a smarter interface. It requires new architecture, agentic compliance and risk controls that preserve human oversight where it matters. Banking 5.0 sets out the case for that transition and what separates structural change from a chatbot layered over legacy systems.
description_zh: 智慧經濟體正開始在交通、能源、商業與金融領域做出決策並採取行動。銀行業的下一波轉變可能隨之而來：AI 代理可能從向客戶提供建議，進一步代客戶發起交易、協調服務並管理財務成果。這種前景引出了一個結構性問題：以人類指令、批次支付及熟悉的問責形式為基礎的系統，能否支援以機器速度運行的金融活動？答案不僅取決於更智慧的介面，還需要新的架構、代理型法遵機制，以及能在關鍵之處保留人類監督的風險控制。「Banking 5.0」將闡述這項轉型的理由，以及真正的結構性變革與在舊有系統上疊加聊天機器人之間的差別。

title: Towards New Operating Models in Financial Services: From Organisation Transformation to Competitive Advantage
description: By 2027, most financial institutions will have adopted the same AI tools—and discovered that tools alone change nothing. The real divide is opening between firms that bolt technology onto legacy structures and those bold enough to rebuild how they actually operate. Org charts, decision rights, and the boundary between human and machine are all up for grabs. Learn how leading institutions are redesigning operating models around AI and agents, what structural changes turn transformation into durable advantage, and where incumbents most often stall.
description_zh: 到 2027 年，多數金融機構都將採用相同的 AI 工具，並發現僅靠工具什麼也改變不了。真正的分野，正出現在把技術附加到舊有架構的企業，與有勇氣重建實際營運方式的企業之間。組織架構、決策權，以及人與機器之間的界線，都有待重新界定。本場將說明領先機構如何圍繞 AI 與代理重新設計營運模式、哪些結構性變革能將轉型化為持久優勢，以及既有業者最常在哪些環節停滯。

title: The Great Big Financial Systems Upgrade: Towards Agentic Infrastructure?
description: Banks are racing toward agentic infrastructure. Few can rebuild core banking, payments and risk management at once without the upgrade itself becoming the systemic risk. As autonomous agents move from pilots into production, institutions face a real choice: accelerate the rebuild, or slow down until controls and supervisors catch up. The panel pressure-tests both paths: what a credible migration sequence looks like, where legacy risk controls break under autonomous decision-making, and when deliberately slowing down is the smarter strategic call rather than a failure of nerve.
description_zh: 銀行正競相邁向代理型基礎設施。然而，鮮少有機構能同時重建核心銀行業務、支付與風險管理，而不讓升級本身成為系統性風險。隨著自主代理從試點進入正式營運，機構面臨真正的抉擇：加速重建，或放慢腳步，等待控制措施與監管者跟上。本場座談將對兩條路徑進行壓力檢驗：可信的遷移順序應是什麼樣貌、舊有風險控制在自主決策下會在哪些地方失效，以及何時刻意放慢腳步是更明智的策略選擇，而非缺乏勇氣。

title: The Autonomous Economy: Where Agentic AI meets Programmable Money
description: Imagine an economy where software doesn't just recommend decisions—it makes them, negotiates them, and settles them, all without a human in the loop. That future arrives when agentic AI meets programmable money. Autonomous agents that can transact, and digital money that can execute logic on its own, together unlock machine-speed commerce that today's financial rails were never built to handle. Learn how agentic AI and programmable money combine to reshape payments, settlement, and value exchange, what new risks emerge when agents transact autonomously, and how institutions should prepare for an economy that runs itself.
description_zh: 想像一個經濟體，軟體不只是提出決策建議，而是自行做出決策、進行協商並完成結算，全程無須人類介入。當代理型 AI 遇上可程式化貨幣，這樣的未來就會到來。能夠交易的自主代理，加上可自行執行邏輯的數位貨幣，共同開啟以機器速度運作的商務，而現今金融軌道在設計之初並未打算處理這種模式。本場將說明代理型 AI 與可程式化貨幣如何結合，重塑支付、結算與價值交換；代理自主交易時會出現哪些新風險；以及機構應如何為自行運作的經濟體做好準備。

title: One World, Many Rails: Defining the Next Chapter of Money Movement
speakers: Brad Garlinghouse; Meagen Burnett; Richard Teng
description: Money moves globally, but the rails beneath it don't speak the same language. Instant payment systems, stablecoins, card networks, correspondent banking, and CBDCs are all racing to define how value crosses borders—and no single winner is emerging. The future isn't one universal rail; it's many, and the real challenge is making them interoperate without friction, fragmentation, or lost trust. Learn how the competing rails of global money movement are converging and colliding, what interoperability actually requires across systems and jurisdictions, and where the next chapter of cross-border payments is really being written.
description_zh: 資金在全球流動，但其底層軌道卻使用不同的語言。即時支付系統、穩定幣、卡組織網絡、通匯銀行業務與央行數位貨幣（CBDC），都在競相定義價值如何跨境流動，但沒有任何一方成為唯一贏家。未來不會只有一條通用軌道，而是多條並存；真正的挑戰是讓它們能夠互通，避免摩擦、碎片化與信任流失。本場將說明全球資金流動中相互競爭的軌道如何融合與碰撞、跨系統及司法管轄區的互通性究竟需要什麼，以及跨境支付的下一篇章實際正在哪裡譜寫。

title: Pay It Forward
description: Whether you're a student starting out, a finance professional planning a career pivot, or a startup founder facing a specific business challenge, Pay It Forward connects you with established industry professionals for face-to-face, one-to-one mentorship. It's a chance to get advice from people who have already worked through the challenges you're facing. Sessions are 15 minutes long and take place at the Pay It Forward Lounge in Hall 3, from 18 to 20 November, 12.30pm to 4.30pm. Come with one specific question or challenge, and leave with focused, practical advice.
description_zh: 無論你是剛起步的學生、計畫轉換職涯方向的金融專業人士，還是面臨特定商業挑戰的新創公司創辦人，Pay It Forward 都能讓你與資深業界專業人士面對面，接受一對一的導師指導。你將有機會向曾經克服你目前所遇挑戰的人請益。每次交流為 15 分鐘，於 11 月 18 日至 20 日下午 12:30 至 4:30，在第 3 展廳的 Pay It Forward Lounge 舉行。帶著一個具體問題或挑戰前來，帶走聚焦且實用的建議。

description: Rewiring the Founder Playbook is where founders, investors, enterprise buyers and policymakers confront the decisions reshaping the next generation of financial companies: who gets funded, what buyers will pay for, which moats survive AI, and when growth should become an exit. Flagship Founders Peak talks reveal the personal stories behind those decisions.
description_zh: 「Rewiring the Founder Playbook」讓創辦人、投資人、企業買家與政策制定者，直面正在重塑下一代金融公司的決策：誰能獲得資金、買家願意為什麼付費、哪些護城河能在 AI 時代存續，以及何時應從追求成長轉向退場。旗艦 Founders Peak 演講將揭示這些決策背後的親身故事。

title: Welcome to Catalyst Stage - Day 2
description: Join us as we kick off the day's sessions on the Catalyst Stage, featuring insightful conversations, groundbreaking ideas, and inspiring voices shaping the next wave of talent and ideas.

title: The Agentic Enterprise: Accountability and Containment When the Machine Decides
speakers: Alan Lim; Casey Klyszeiko; Colin Payne; Richard Tong; Irene Liu
description:
Agentic AI has moved from pilots to systems that touch real credit decisions, real client money and real compliance rules, and the institutions getting the governance right this year are setting the ceiling for the next decade. This session examines where accountability sits once an agent, not a person, initiates the action, across risk, audit and reporting lines — and then confronts the scenario most institutions would rather not discuss: what actually happens in the moments after an agent goes wrong.

An agent doesn't take a coffee break. When it fails, it can fail at machine speed, across every transaction it touches, before a human even notices. So the real test isn't whether agents fail, but how fast an institution can contain them when they do, and who is authorised to make that call. This discussion moves from the accountability question to the operational one: what real-time containment looks like in practice, where autonomous systems are most likely to break, and how to build the kill switches and safeguards that limit the blast radius before autonomy is extended any further.

Attendees leave with a sharper view of the controls that need to exist before autonomy is extended further. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: Who is accountable when an autonomous agent makes a bad call, moves client money, or silently breaks a compliance rule?
description_zh: 代理型 AI 已從試點走向涉及真實信貸決策、真實客戶資金與實際法遵規則的系統，而今年能做好治理的機構，正為未來十年奠定發展上限。本場將檢視，一旦發起行動的是代理而非人，在風險、稽核與匯報體系中，責任應歸於何處；接著直面多數機構寧可不談的情境：代理出錯後的最初幾個瞬間，究竟會發生什麼？代理不會休息喝咖啡。當它失效時，可能在人類察覺之前，就以機器速度在所接觸的每筆交易中接連出錯。因此，真正的考驗不在於代理是否會失效，而在於機構能多快控制失效的代理，以及誰獲授權做出這個決定。本場討論將從問責問題轉向營運問題：即時遏制在實務中是什麼樣貌、自主系統最可能在哪些地方出問題，以及如何在進一步擴大自主權之前，建立緊急停用機制與防護措施，以限制影響範圍。與會者將更清楚了解，在進一步擴大自主權之前，必須具備哪些控制措施。本場座談將深入探討的一個關鍵問題是：當自主代理做出錯誤判斷、移動客戶資金，或悄悄違反法遵規則時，誰應負責？

title: One Network, Millions of Bills, Billions of Live: The Infrastructure Behind Interoperable Bill Payments - Powered by NPCI
description: Bharat Connect is an interoperable bill payment system, the only platform across the globe to enable millions of customers for paying their utility bills. This session will cover the impact of the infrastructure and the effect it has on utility service providers.
description_zh: Bharat Connect 是一套可互通的帳單支付系統，也是全球唯一能讓數百萬名客戶繳付公用事業帳單的平台。本場將介紹這項基礎設施所帶來的影響，以及它對公用事業服務提供者的作用。

title: Money is programmable. Can Tokenized Markets follow?
speakers: Gracie Lin; Stephen Richardson; Carolyn Weinberg; Dr. Tara Rice; Emma Joyce
description: For decades, financial innovation meant new products on old rails. That lens no longer explains where control is concentrating. Money 1.0 digitised value. Money 2.0 networked it. Money 3.0 makes it programmable — value that carries its own logic, constraints and compliance, settling toward atomic, with AI agents as first-class transactors. But is this a structural shift, or digitisation in new clothes? This opening session looks to separate architecture from hype and asks the question that matters: How far can programmable money along with tokenized financial products go?
description_zh: 數十年來，金融創新意味著在舊軌道上推出新產品。這種視角已無法解釋控制權正在向何處集中。Money 1.0 將價值數位化；Money 2.0 將其網絡化；Money 3.0 則使其可程式化，讓價值自帶邏輯、限制與法遵規則，結算朝原子化邁進，並將 AI 代理視為具有完整地位的交易主體。但這究竟是結構性轉變，還是換了新裝的數位化？本場開場議程將嘗試區分真正的架構與炒作，並提出關鍵問題：可程式化貨幣與代幣化金融產品，究竟能走多遠？

title: Is Shared Risk and Outcome-Based Pricing the Only Way Enterprises Will Now Buy?
description: Corporate technology leaders are increasingly rejecting per-user subscription licenses that divorce vendor fees from measurable client performance. Research from Deloitte’s Global Chief Procurement Officer Survey indicates that 58% of enterprise procurement executives are prioritizing shared-risk, outcome-contingent commercial contracts across new software implementations to curtail budget creep. However, structuring these arrangements without triggering legal disputes requires objective measurement standards. This session explores how enterprise buyers and vendors structure verifiable performance baselines, downside penalties, and margin-protected upside mechanisms to deploy sustainable, outcome-based software engagements across mission-critical enterprise systems.
description_zh: 企業科技領導者愈來愈不願接受按使用者計費的訂閱授權，因為這種模式使供應商收費與可衡量的客戶績效脫鉤。勤業眾信《全球採購長調查》的研究指出，58% 的企業採購主管正優先在新軟體導入中採用風險共擔、以成果為條件的商業合約，以抑制預算不斷膨脹。然而，要在不引發法律爭議的情況下設計這些安排，需要客觀的衡量標準。本場探討企業買家與供應商如何設計可驗證的績效基準、未達標懲罰，以及保護利潤率的超額成果獎勵機制，從而在攸關企業關鍵任務的系統中，建立可持續、以成果為基礎的軟體合作關係。

title: Scaling AI: Where Financial Services is Seeing Real Returns
speakers: Abhijeet Ramesh; Mayoran Rajendra; Quan Yu; Dr. David Hardoon
description:
The conversation around AI in financial services has moved beyond experimentation. The challenge is no longer identifying promising use cases—it's deploying AI at scale in ways that deliver measurable business value. From payments and banking to fintech and customer engagement, leading institutions are embedding AI into core operations to improve productivity, strengthen risk management, personalise customer experiences, and accelerate innovation. Yet while some initiatives become enterprise capabilities, many others remain trapped in pilot mode.

Bringing together leaders from across the financial services ecosystem, this panel explores where AI is creating tangible impact today, what it takes to scale successful deployments across the organisation, and the operational, cultural, and governance challenges that determine whether AI delivers lasting value. The discussion will examine how institutions are prioritising AI investments, measuring success beyond productivity gains, and building the data, operating models, and organisational capabilities needed to move from isolated use cases to enterprise-wide transformation.
description_zh: 金融服務領域有關 AI 的討論已超越試驗階段。挑戰不再是找出有潛力的使用情境，而是以能帶來可衡量商業價值的方式，大規模部署 AI。從支付與銀行業務，到金融科技與客戶互動，領先機構正將 AI 嵌入核心營運，以提高生產力、強化風險管理、提供個人化客戶體驗並加速創新。然而，部分計畫雖然已成為企業能力，許多其他計畫卻仍困在試點階段。本場座談匯聚金融服務生態系各領域的領導者，探討 AI 如今在哪些方面帶來實質影響、如何將成功部署擴展至整個組織，以及哪些營運、文化與治理挑戰，決定 AI 能否創造持久價值。討論將檢視各機構如何排定 AI 投資的優先順序、如何在生產力提升之外衡量成功，以及如何建立必要的資料、營運模式與組織能力，從零散的使用情境走向全企業轉型。

title: Tokenization at Scale: From Pilot to On Chain Money Movement - Powered by J.P. Morgan
description: Tokenization is moving from pilots to production. In 15 minutes, we’ll share what corporates, asset managers, FIs and fintechs need to adopt on chain money movement: where value is real, what risks show up in production, and the operating controls that unlock scale, grounded in real-world tokenized payments and tokenized fund examples.
description_zh: 代幣化正從試點走向正式營運。在 15 分鐘內，我們將透過真實世界的代幣化支付與代幣化基金案例，分享企業、資產管理公司、金融機構與金融科技公司採用鏈上資金流動所需了解的事項：真正的價值在哪裡、正式營運時會出現哪些風險，以及哪些營運控制能促成規模化。

title: Stablecoins, Tokenized Deposits, Tokenized MMF and CBDCs: Which Money Earns a Place in the Stack?
description: Stablecoins, tokenised deposits, tokenised MMFs and CBDCs are all racing to become the default form of institutional money, though none of them do the same job equally well. Four advocates, one per instrument get two minutes each to pitch to our moderator, who presses each on the trade-offs. Then the audience votes: what would you actually hold for payroll, for treasury, for cross-border? Come find out what counts as money when the answer depends on the job.
description_zh: 穩定幣、代幣化存款、代幣化貨幣市場基金（MMF）及央行數位貨幣（CBDC）都在競逐成為機構資金的預設形式，但它們執行同一項任務的能力並不相同。四位倡議者分別代表一種工具，各有兩分鐘向主持人推介，主持人則會追問各自的取捨。接著由觀眾投票：支付薪資、財務管理及跨境交易時，你實際上會持有哪一種？當答案取決於用途時，一起來探討什麼才算是貨幣。

title: Have We Come to the End of Anonymous Ownership for Regulated Digital Assets? - Powered by Cleanverse
description: As TradFi moves on-chain, can ownership of regulated digital assets remain anonymous? Programmed Governance offers a new model where trusted identity, asset eligibility and policy rules are checked and validated before value moves. As money becomes programmable, this session explores the next frontier: rewiring policy for an era of programmable value.
description_zh: 隨著傳統金融（TradFi）走向鏈上，受監管數位資產的所有權還能保持匿名嗎？程式化治理（Programmed Governance）提出一種新模式，在價值轉移之前先檢查並驗證可信身分、資產資格及政策規則。當貨幣變得可程式化，本場次將探索下一個前沿：為可程式化價值時代重塑政策。

title: AI & Core Banking: Who Builds the Machine, Who Regulates it? Core Banking's New Compliance Perimeter
description:
Core banking functions such as credit decisions, trade finance, fraud detection and KYC are shifting from pilot demonstrations into live, algorithm-driven workflows, and the institutions pulling ahead are rebuilding these processes end to end rather than adding AI on top of what already exists.

This session brings together the people actually doing that rebuild - the platforms it runs on, the institutions deploying it, and the regulators overseeing it - to work through what that rebuild actually requires: which controls move from human sign-off to automated checkpoints, and where the audit trail needs redesigning rather than retrofitting.
description_zh: 信貸決策、貿易融資、詐欺偵測及認識你的客戶（KYC）等核心銀行業務，正從試點展示轉向由演算法驅動的正式工作流程。領先的機構正在端到端重建這些流程，而不是在既有系統上附加 AI。本場次匯聚真正參與重建的人，包括支撐流程的平台、部署流程的機構及負責監督的監管機關，共同探討重建實際需要什麼：哪些控管措施要從人工簽核轉為自動化檢查點，以及哪些稽核軌跡需要重新設計，而非事後改裝。

title: Beyond the Product Stack: Platform as the New Advantage in Banking - Powered by Veefin Solutions
description: Banks have spent a decade buying products like Cash management, Trade Finance, Supply Chain Finance, Lending; and stitching them together afterwards. The cost isn't just efficiency; it caps growth: fragmented data, duplicated workflows, and change that moves at the pace of the slowest system. This session argues that banking's next competitive advantage is architectural, and shows what institutions building on one foundation do differently
description_zh: 過去十年，銀行不斷採購現金管理、貿易融資、供應鏈融資及放款等產品，再將它們拼接起來。代價不只是效率下降，也限制了成長：資料零散、工作流程重複，而變革速度受最慢的系統牽制。本場次主張，銀行業下一個競爭優勢在於架構，並展示以單一基礎建設業務的機構有哪些不同做法。

title: Liquidity Fragmentation: Tokenization's Hidden Risk - Powered by Hedera Foundry Inc
description: Tokenization pilots keep succeeding technically and failing to scale, because liquidity fragments across a dozen new rails instead of moving as one. This session makes the case that fragmentation, not technology, is the real risk institutions face next, and shows what banks moving past the pilot stage are actually doing differently to solve it.
description_zh: 代幣化試點在技術上屢屢成功，卻無法擴大規模，原因是流動性分散在十多條新的基礎通道，而未能整體流動。本場次將說明，機構接下來面臨的真正風險是碎片化，而非技術，並展示已跨越試點階段的銀行實際採取了哪些不同做法來解決這個問題。

title: RWA Tokenization: From Products to Liquid Markets
speakers: Chris Yin; Fiona Murray; Kazuya Ikeda; Delane Foo
description: RWA tokenisation has a surplus of vision and a shortage of honest post-mortems. This session is the latter. Which asset classes are seeing real traction, and which are stuck in pilot theatre? How much settlement has actually been compressed and what breaks in the transition? Tokenised collateral promises mobility the legacy system can't match, but only if the legal frameworks hold. The question for banks, financial institutions and asset managers: who are the new investors, and what do they need to see before they allocate? Practitioners who have shipped and carry the scars, separate the working from the wished-for.
description_zh: 現實世界資產（RWA）代幣化不缺願景，缺的是坦誠的事後檢討。本場次正是這樣的檢討。哪些資產類別真正獲得市場採用，哪些仍停留在試點展示？結算時間實際縮短了多少，轉型過程又有哪些環節失靈？代幣化擔保品有望提供傳統系統無法比擬的流動能力，但前提是法律架構必須站得住腳。銀行、金融機構及資產管理業者要問的是：新投資人是誰，他們在配置資金前需要看到什麼？真正推出過產品、也承受過挫折的實務工作者，將分辨哪些做法確實有效，哪些仍只是期望。

title: Connecting Global SMEs: How Financial Institutions Scale Cross-border Markets with XTransfer - Powered by XTransfer Limited
description: As trade corridors shift and USD liquidity tightens, SMEs are moving into new markets faster than financial institutions can keep up. This session explores what's changing on the ground and how banks can support SME growth across emerging-market corridors and beyond.
description_zh: 隨著貿易走廊轉移及美元流動性收緊，中小企業進入新市場的速度已超過金融機構跟進的步伐。本場次探討第一線正在發生的變化，以及銀行如何支持中小企業在新興市場走廊及更廣泛市場中的成長。

title: Rewiring Global Payments: Building the Infrastructure for a More Connected Commerce Economy - Powered by NTT DATA
description: Commerce no longer stops at borders, but much of the infrastructure behind it still does. As commerce becomes increasingly digital, cross-border and interconnected, we are seeing greater convergence across payment networks, technology and local ecosystems. What will it take to bridge these divides and build payments infrastructure that is secure, scalable and capable of supporting the next generation of commerce?
description_zh: 商業活動已不再受國界限制，但支撐它的許多基礎設施仍然如此。隨著商業愈來愈數位化、跨境化且相互連結，支付網路、技術與在地生態系也更加融合。要彌合這些落差，打造安全、可擴充且能支援下一代商業的支付基礎設施，需要具備哪些條件？

title: What Evidence Will Investors Seek to Issue a Term Sheet in 2027?
description: Investor conviction has shifted decisively away from TAM projections and charismatic narrative pitching. According to Carta's Private Market Round Diligence Metrics, institutional closing timelines expanded by 45% as investment committees demand audited proofs: net revenue retention above 120% and gross profit margins exceeding 70% before term sheets are issued. The threshold to secure lead capital requires verifiable customer engagement rather than pilot commitments. This session convenes prominent venture partners to reveal the specific retention cohorts, contract architectures, and defensibility milestones that genuinely command high-conviction checks in the current market.
description_zh: 投資人的信心基礎已明確轉向，不再依靠總體潛在市場（TAM）預測及富有感染力的故事式募資簡報。根據 Carta 的私募市場融資輪盡職調查指標，機構完成交易所需時間延長了 45%，因為投資委員會要求在發出投資條款書前，提供經查核的證據：淨營收留存率高於 120%，毛利率超過 70%。取得領投資金的門檻是可驗證的客戶參與，而非試點承諾。本場次邀集知名創投合夥人，揭示在當前市場中，究竟哪些具體的留存客群、合約架構及競爭防禦力里程碑，能真正贏得投資人高度確信的資金投入。

title: When Agents Direct Agents: Who Do You Actually Regulate?
description:
Financial regulation has always assumed that decisions can be traced through a clear chain of human accountability. But as AI agents begin directing other agents, that assumption starts to break down. Agentic AI won't just automate tasks—it has the potential to reshape how financial institutions are organised. Decision-making may shift between people and AI systems, reporting lines become more fluid, and the traditional structures underpinning governance, accountability and supervision begin to evolve. In that world, who is ultimately responsible for a decision? What exactly is a regulator supervising?

Bringing together senior policymakers and regulators, this session explores how supervisory frameworks—from senior manager accountability regimes to board oversight and the three lines of defence—need to adapt for organisations where humans increasingly govern systems that, in turn, govern other systems. The discussion will examine how institutions can demonstrate accountability, maintain effective oversight, and provide regulators with meaningful traceability in increasingly agent-driven operating models. Rather than focusing on individual AI decisions, the panel asks a broader question: how should governance evolve when the organisation itself becomes dynamic?
description_zh: 金融監管一直假設，決策可以沿著清楚的人類責任鏈追溯。然而，隨著 AI 代理開始指揮其他代理，這項假設正逐漸失效。代理型 AI 不只會自動化任務，也可能重塑金融機構的組織方式。決策權可能在人員與 AI 系統之間移轉，匯報關係變得更具流動性，支撐治理、問責及監理的傳統結構也開始演變。在這樣的世界裡，誰對決策負最終責任？監管機關究竟在監督什麼？本場次匯聚資深政策制定者與監管者，探討從高階主管問責制度、董事會監督到三道防線的監理架構，應如何因應這類組織：人類愈來愈多地治理系統，而系統又治理其他系統。討論將檢視，在日益由代理驅動的營運模式中，機構如何證明責任歸屬、維持有效監督，並向監管機關提供有實質意義的可追溯性。本場論壇不只聚焦個別 AI 決策，更提出一個廣泛的問題：當組織本身變得動態，治理應如何演進？

title: Trust by Design: Building the Future of Digital Assets in Asia - Powered by Coinbase
description: As digital assets become increasingly integrated into the financial system, trust is becoming a competitive advantage. What does it take to build digital-asset infrastructure that consumers, businesses and institutions can rely on?
description_zh: 隨著數位資產愈來愈深入金融體系，信任正成為一項競爭優勢。要打造消費者、企業及機構都能信賴的數位資產基礎設施，需要具備哪些條件？

title: Who Owns the Moment an Agent Decides to Pay?
description: Your next customer won't be human. AI agents are becoming first-class transactors — browsing, deciding and paying with no person in the loop. When software initiates the payment, the contest shifts from the rail to the moment of intent: who owns it — the wallet, the platform, the merchant, or the agent's operator? What does an agent need before it can spend: identity, mandate, limits, recourse? Why do stablecoins and programmable money fit machine-initiated commerce better than card rails built for humans? And when an agent pays the wrong party on the wrong instruction, who is liable? The checkout is being rebuilt for machines. This session is about who gets to own it.
description_zh: 你的下一位客戶將不是人類。AI 代理正在成為獨立的交易主體，在無人介入的情況下瀏覽、決策及付款。當付款由軟體發起，競爭焦點便從支付通道轉向意圖形成的那一刻：究竟由誰掌握，是錢包、平台、商家，還是代理的營運者？代理在支出前需要哪些條件：身分、授權、限額及追索途徑？為什麼穩定幣與可程式化貨幣比為人類設計的卡片支付通道，更適合由機器發起的商業活動？當代理依據錯誤指令付款給錯誤對象時，又該由誰承擔責任？結帳流程正為機器重新打造。本場次探討誰能掌握這個環節。

title: YTP-AIF Presentation & Panel: Skills and Talent Development for GenAI
description:
As GenAI reshapes finance, the decisive constraint isn't the technology—it's talent. Do institutions have the skills, and the pipeline, to keep pace? This session pairs a candid industry dialogue on the widening GenAI capability gap with a showcase of YTP-AIF finalist projects, where students present real AI solutions built for finance.

You will learn: where the most urgent skills shortfalls are emerging, how institutions are building GenAI-ready talent, and where the next generation is already placing its bets. A look at both sides of the talent equation—the gap, and the people who will close it.
description_zh: 生成式 AI（GenAI）正在重塑金融業，而決定性的限制因素是人才，不是技術。機構是否具備足夠的技能與人才供給，能跟上變化？本場次結合業界對日益擴大的 GenAI 能力落差的坦誠對話，以及 YTP-AIF 決賽入圍專案展示，由學生介紹為金融業打造的實際 AI 解決方案。你將了解：最迫切的技能缺口出現在哪裡、機構如何培養具備 GenAI 能力的人才，以及新一代已將投入重點放在哪些領域。一同檢視人才問題的兩面：缺口，以及將填補缺口的人。

title: Beyond Payments: Own the Journey, Not the Fleet - Powered by ELIFE & HOPPA
description: A hotel concierge earns trust by arranging the journey, not owning the car. This session asks what banks and wallets can learn from that model. Through examples from super-apps, digital banks and behaviour-based rewards programmes, it explores how embedded mobility can drive revenue and loyalty. Participants will leave with a practical framework for testing the economics and safeguarding trust when partners deliver the service.
description_zh: 飯店禮賓人員透過安排旅程贏得信任，而不是靠擁有車輛。本場次探討銀行與錢包可以從這種模式學到什麼，並透過超級應用程式、數位銀行及以行為為基礎的獎勵計畫案例，說明嵌入式交通服務如何帶動營收及忠誠度。與會者將獲得一套實用架構，用於在合作夥伴提供服務時，檢驗經濟效益並維護信任。

title: Digital Autonomy in AI: Optionality Over Absolute Independence
speakers: Dr. Joseph Breeden; Prof. Dr. Fritzi Köhler-Geib; Steven Maijoor; Sunayna Tuteja
description:
No bank can or should build every AI capability itself. The real strategic question isn't build versus buy; it's whether institutions retain meaningful choice over the technology they depend on. As agentic AI begins making decisions that affect customers, capital, and risk, financial institutions must ask: How much digital dependency is acceptable? Can they trust and explain the decision of models they didn't build? What happens when the AI underpinning critical operations is controlled by a single provider?

The panel explores what digital autonomy should look like in the AI era. Rather than arguing for complete self-sufficiency, the discussion focuses on optionality: the ability to choose between providers, maintain control over sensitive data, satisfy regulatory expectations for explainability, and preserve resilient fallback options when business or technology priorities change. The conversation will examine how banks can adopt AI at scale without sacrificing transparency, governance or strategic independence - and why genuine optionality may become one of the industry's most important competitive advantages.
description_zh: 沒有一家銀行能夠或應該自行打造所有 AI 能力。真正的策略問題不是自建或採購，而是機構是否對其所依賴的技術保有實質選擇權。隨著代理型 AI 開始做出影響客戶、資本及風險的決策，金融機構必須問：多大程度的數位依賴可以接受？對於並非自行建立的模型所做的決策，是否能夠信任並加以解釋？當支撐關鍵營運的 AI 由單一供應商控制時，會發生什麼事？本場論壇探討 AI 時代的數位自主應有何種樣貌。討論不以完全自給自足為訴求，而是聚焦選擇空間：能在供應商之間選擇、維持對敏感資料的控制、滿足監管機關對可解釋性的期待，以及在業務或技術優先順序改變時，保留具有韌性的備援選項。對話將檢視銀行如何在不犧牲透明度、治理或策略獨立性的前提下，大規模採用 AI，以及為何真正的選擇權可能成為業界最重要的競爭優勢之一。

title: What Makes Tokenization Production-Ready?
speakers: Domenico Nardelli; Salim Dhanani; Jael Tan
description: Tokenization doesn't fail on vision. It fails on plumbing. Behind every live corridor sits an unglamorous stack that decides whether it scales. Which settlement layer — L1, L2 or private and at what trade-off? How do you achieve legal finality across jurisdictions that don't agree? Which interoperability standards actually matter, and who is driving them? This session decodes the replicable components behind the case studies — the decisions that separate a production system from an expensive proof-of-concept.
description_zh: 代幣化失敗的原因不是願景，而是底層基礎設施。每一條正式運作的走廊背後，都有一套不起眼卻決定其能否擴大規模的技術架構。該選擇哪種結算層：L1、L2 還是私有鏈，又各有什麼取捨？如何在意見不一致的司法管轄區之間達成法律上的最終性？哪些互通標準真正重要，又由誰推動？本場次將解析案例研究背後可複製的組成要素，探討哪些決策讓系統得以正式投入生產，而不只是昂貴的概念驗證。

title: Agentic Payments: Are Our Rails Ready?
description:
For decades, payment systems have been designed around human behaviour. AI agents play by different rules. Unlike humans, agents do not care about rewards, interfaces or brand loyalty. They optimise for speed, cost, and reliability.

As agents begin making payments on behalf of users and businesses, they may transact at a scale and frequency never seen before, paying for everything from AI services and digital content to machine-to-machine interactions. The result could be millions of low-value transactions that challenge the economics and design of today's payment infrastructure.

Are our payment rails ready for this future? As PayNow Gen2 considers capabilities relevant to agentic commerce, this session explores whether existing payment rails can adapt, what role programmable money could play, and how payment infrastructure must evolve when machines start choosing how to pay.
description_zh: 幾十年來，支付系統一直圍繞人類行為設計。AI 代理卻遵循不同規則。與人類不同，代理不在意獎勵、介面或品牌忠誠度，而是追求速度、成本及可靠性的最佳化。當代理開始代表使用者及企業付款，它們可能以前所未有的規模與頻率進行交易，支付範圍從 AI 服務、數位內容到機器對機器互動。結果可能是數以百萬計的小額交易，挑戰現有支付基礎設施的經濟模式與設計。我們的支付通道準備好迎接這樣的未來了嗎？隨著 PayNow Gen2 考量代理型商業所需的相關能力，本場次將探討既有支付通道能否調整、可程式化貨幣可以扮演什麼角色，以及當機器開始自行選擇付款方式時，支付基礎設施必須如何演進。

title: Will Radical Downsizing Your Startup Break the Machine or Unlock Growth in 2027?
description: The venture doctrine equating organizational headcount with enterprise valuation has permanently broken down. After Klarna leveraged AI automation to trim its workforce from 5,000 toward 2,000 employees, its annual revenue per employee surged over 70% alongside a return to profitability. Meanwhile, ultra-lean software firms like Linear capped their full-time team under 50 while scaling past tens of millions in ARR. This session explores the operational balance of deep workforce restructuring: identifying which functions to automate permanently, where human domain expertise is indispensable, and which specialized hires must be recruited immediately.
description_zh: 將組織員工人數與企業估值畫上等號的創投信條，已經永久失效。Klarna 利用 AI 自動化，將員工人數從 5,000 人朝 2,000 人縮減後，每位員工的年營收大增逾 70%，公司也恢復獲利。與此同時，Linear 等極精簡的軟體公司，將全職團隊控制在 50 人以下，年度經常性收入（ARR）卻已成長至數千萬以上。本場次探討大幅重整人力時的營運平衡：辨識哪些職能應永久自動化、哪些領域仍不可或缺地需要人類專業，以及哪些專業人才必須立即招募。

title: Governance-by-Design: Can compliance move at the speed of code?
speakers: Ari Redbord; Ceridwen Choo; Gary Liu
description: The more money behaves like software, the more the decisive questions become legal and political rather than technical. Who is liable when a smart contract executes exactly as written and wrongly? How do sanctions and AML function when compliance is embedded in code rather than checked after the fact? What does systemic resilience mean when value moves at machine speed and a flawed rule can propagate across the system in a single run cycle? We will close the track with the question programmable money must answer to earn its licence: governance-by-design or not at all.
description_zh: 當貨幣愈來愈像軟體，決定性的問題就愈偏向法律與政治，而非技術。智慧合約完全依照程式碼執行，卻產生錯誤結果時，由誰承擔責任？當法遵嵌入程式碼，而不是事後檢查，制裁與洗錢防制（AML）該如何運作？當價值以機器速度流動，一條有缺陷的規則可在單次執行週期內傳遍整個系統，系統性韌性又意味著什麼？本主題軌將以可程式化貨幣必須回答、才能獲准運作的問題作結：治理必須納入設計，否則便無從談起。

title: PolyFinTech100 API Hackathon
The Price of Connection: What It Actually Takes to Build Cross-Border Payment Cooperation
speakers: Joyce Bo; Sohini Rajola; Andrew McCormack; Carlos Álvarez
description:
Every institution talks about the need for interoperability but few speak honestly about what it actually costs, in regulation, in pricing, and in the multilateral negotiation it takes to connect one country's payment system to another's. This panel brings together the messaging networks, reserve-pooling mechanisms, national schemes and multilateral hubs doing this work in practice, to work through the frictions: which regulatory frameworks still block genuine interoperability, how the economics of a cross-border link actually get split between the parties that build and operate it, and what a smaller or newer market needs in place before it can plug into a bigger one.

This panel aims to present a grounded view of where multilateral payment cooperation is actually working today, what it costs to get there and dive deeper into whether the real barrier to cross-border payment connectivity is technical, regulatory or commercial.
description_zh: 每家機構都談論互通性的必要性，卻很少坦誠談及其真正成本，包括監管、定價，以及連結兩國支付系統所需的多邊協商。本場論壇匯聚實際投入這項工作的訊息傳輸網路、儲備資金共用機制、國家支付體系及多邊樞紐，共同梳理各項阻力：哪些監管架構仍阻礙真正的互通性、跨境連結的成本與收益實際上如何在建置及營運各方之間分配，以及規模較小或較新的市場，在接入較大市場之前需要具備哪些條件。本場論壇希望務實呈現今日多邊支付合作真正有效的領域、達成合作所需的成本，並深入探討跨境支付互聯的真正障礙究竟在於技術、監管，還是商業因素。

title: Balance Sheet Strategy in Money 3.0
speakers: Emma Hagan; George Davis; Nischint Sanghavi; Kirit Bhatia
description: For CFOs and treasurers, programmable money is not a thesis, it's an allocation decision. Where does settlement risk really sit when value moves in real time, and who carries the exposure? How does tokenisation rewrite collateral management and intraday liquidity? What does the yield/risk trade-off look like across deposits and other forms of money, and what happens to deposit insurance and the lender of last resort when money is code? The question boards are starting to ask: whose balance sheet does each instrument sit on, yours, your bank's, or nobody's? And are balance sheet light banking models the safer answer? A working session for the people who answer with real money.
description_zh: 對財務長及財務主管而言，可程式化貨幣不是一套論述，而是資金配置決策。當價值即時移轉，結算風險究竟存在於哪裡，又由誰承擔曝險？代幣化如何改變擔保品管理及日內流動性？存款與其他貨幣形式之間的收益與風險取捨如何？當貨幣化為程式碼，存款保險及最後貸款人制度又會如何？董事會開始提出的問題是：每種工具究竟列在誰的資產負債表上，是你自己的、你的銀行的，還是不屬於任何人？而輕資產負債表的銀行模式，是否是更安全的答案？這是一場為必須以真金白銀作答的人設計的實務討論。

title: Financing Financial Infrastructure in Emerging Markets
description:
Building the infrastructure for financial inclusion and cross-border connectivity is one challenge. Financing it is another, and it's the one that usually gets skipped over in the excitement about what could be built. Is the binding constraint on financial inclusion the technology, or the capital to build and sustain it?

This panel brings together leaders from a small economy building its own digital public infrastructure, a hub positioning itself to draw global capital into a fast-growing regional market, and a development bank whose entire mandate is getting credit to populations mainstream finance still doesn't reach. The dialogue will focus on where the funding for this actually comes from, state budgets, development finance, or private capital drawn in by the right market positioning, and what it takes for a smaller or developing market to make itself genuinely investable.
description_zh: 建置普惠金融與跨境互聯的基礎設施是一項挑戰，為它籌措資金則是另一項。而每當人們熱烈討論可以建造什麼時，資金問題往往被略過。制約普惠金融的關鍵究竟是技術，還是建置並維持運作所需的資本？本場論壇匯聚多方領導者：正在打造自身數位公共基礎設施的小型經濟體、致力吸引全球資本進入快速成長區域市場的樞紐，以及以向主流金融仍未觸及的人群提供信貸為使命的開發銀行。對話將聚焦這些資金實際從何而來，包括國家預算、開發融資，或透過適當市場定位吸引的民間資本，以及較小型或發展中市場需要具備哪些條件，才能真正成為值得投資的對象。

title: How to Evaluate a Strategic Exit vs. Continuing to Build?
description: With conventional IPO pathways narrowed and growth-stage liquidity constrained, many companies must re-evaluate what a successful outcome looks like. Crunchbase's 2026 M&A Outlook recorded 36 unicorn M&A exits worth a combined $67B in 2025, and EY-Parthenon reports teams under 100 people landing $100M+ acqui-hire exits. An early acqui-hire or IP sale can preserve talent and technological value, but requires careful negotiation. This session outlines the operational indicators and timing indicators founders need to weigh a structured exit against continuing to build.
description_zh: 隨著傳統首次公開募股（IPO）途徑收窄，成長階段企業的流動性受限，許多公司必須重新評估何謂成功的結果。Crunchbase 的《2026 年併購展望》記錄了 2025 年 36 起獨角獸企業透過併購退出的交易，總值達 670 億美元；EY-Parthenon 則指出，少於 100 人的團隊也能透過人才收購取得逾 1 億美元的退出成果。及早進行人才收購或出售智慧財產權，可以保留人才及技術價值，但需要謹慎協商。本場次將說明創辦人在衡量有規劃的退出與繼續打造事業之間，應考慮哪些營運及時機指標。

title: Geoeconomics of Tokens: Lessons From Live Cross-Border Tokenized Corridors
speakers: Alan Lim; Fernando Vázquez; Oli Harris; Angela Ang
description: Cross-border tokenized corridors are moving from proof-of-concept to production. Hear from the people who made the crossing: what broke first - tech, legal or liquidity; what the operating model actually looks like when someone has to issue, settle and supervise; what they would never build again; and the honest timeline from pilot to scaled corridor. This discussion will be around the gating factors, the requirements, and what it really takes to move live value across borders on tokenised rails.
description_zh: 跨境代幣化走廊正從概念驗證邁向正式運作。聽聽已跨越這道門檻的人分享：最先出問題的是技術、法律還是流動性；當有人必須負責發行、結算及監督時，實際營運模式是什麼樣貌；哪些東西他們絕不會再打造一次；以及從試點走向具規模走廊的真實時程。這場討論將聚焦關鍵制約因素、必要條件，以及透過代幣化基礎通道跨境移轉真實價值究竟需要什麼。

title: Welcome to Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 - Day 3
description: Join us as we kick off the day's sessions on the Festival Stage, featuring insightful conversations, groundbreaking ideas, and inspiring voices shaping the future of FinTech.
description_zh: 加入我們，一同揭開 Festival Stage 當日議程的序幕，聆聽深具洞見的對話、突破性構想，以及塑造金融科技未來的啟發性聲音。

title: Navigating a Capital Rupture: Reallocation, Breakages and Deployment
description: Capital is on the move like never before. As geopolitical fault lines harden, monetary regimes shift, and private markets swell past public ones, the old channels for allocating capital are breaking—and trillions are being redirected in the process. Where money flows, who controls it, and how quickly it can be deployed are all being rewritten. This isn't a market cycle; it's a structural rupture. Learn how capital is being reallocated across regions, asset classes, and public-private lines, where the breakages in traditional deployment are creating risk and opportunity, and what it takes to move decisively in a fractured landscape.
description_zh: 資本正以前所未有的方式流動。隨著地緣政治裂痕加深、貨幣體制轉變，以及私募市場規模膨脹並超越公開市場，舊有的資本配置管道正在瓦解，數兆資金也因此改道。資金流向何處、由誰控制，以及能以多快的速度投入運用，都正在被改寫。這不是市場循環，而是結構性斷裂。了解資本如何跨區域、資產類別及公私市場界線重新配置、傳統資金部署的斷點在哪些地方帶來風險與機會，以及如何在分裂的局勢中果斷行動。

title: Beyond Payments: Building the Economic Infrastructure for AI
description: We built payment systems for humans—accounts, cards, and checkout flows designed around people clicking "buy." But AI agents don't shop that way. As autonomous systems begin to transact, negotiate, and settle at machine speed, they expose how much of our economic infrastructure simply wasn't built for them. Payments are just the surface; identity, trust, contracts, and settlement all need reinventing. Learn what economic infrastructure AI agents actually require beyond payment rails, how identity and trust must evolve when machines transact autonomously, and who is building the foundational layers of the agentic economy.
description_zh: 我們為人類打造支付系統，帳戶、卡片及結帳流程都圍繞人們點選「購買」而設計。但 AI 代理並不這樣購物。當自主系統開始以機器速度交易、協商及結算，它們揭示了我們的經濟基礎設施有多大一部分根本不是為它們而建。支付只是表面，身分、信任、合約及結算都需要重新構想。了解除了支付通道之外，AI 代理究竟需要哪些經濟基礎設施、機器自主交易時身分與信任必須如何演進，以及誰正在建構代理經濟的基礎層。

title: The Great Coordination: Managing Regulatory Multiplicity
speakers: H.E. Chea Serey; Piero Cipollone; Maha El Dimachki
description: Policy rewiring is about who moves fastest inside the gaps between rules. Regulatory strategy is now a competitive advantage, not just a compliance requirement, as sandboxes and new frameworks spread unevenly. This panel looks at how institutions manage that multiplicity, from cross-border cooperation to interoperable supervision. The key question it looks to answer: can regimes never designed to talk to each other coordinate fast enough to keep up with innovation?
description_zh: 政策重塑的重點在於：誰能在規則的縫隙之間動得最快。隨著沙盒與新框架不均勻地擴散，監理策略如今是一種競爭優勢，而不只是法遵要求。本場座談探討機構如何應對這種多重性，從跨境合作到可互通的監督機制。它想回答的關鍵問題是：一套從未被設計成能彼此對話的監理體制，協調的速度跟得上創新嗎？

title: Beyond the Rails: Where Payments Value Is Really Created
speakers: Anuj Khosla; Stephen Karpin; Yukinobu Saeki; Shinichiro Nishikawa
description: For years, payments competed on the rails—faster, cheaper, more reliable ways to move money from A to B. But as transactions become instant, ubiquitous, and nearly free, the rails themselves are commoditizing. The value is migrating elsewhere: to data, embedded experiences, working capital, fraud intelligence, and the software wrapped around every transaction. Moving money is table stakes; the real margin lives above it. Learn where payments value is genuinely being created as core processing commoditizes, how leading players monetize data, software, and embedded finance beyond the transaction, and what it takes to climb the value stack.
description_zh: 多年來，支付競爭聚焦於基礎通道，設法更快速、更便宜且更可靠地把資金從 A 點移到 B 點。但隨著交易變得即時、無所不在且幾乎免費，通道本身正走向同質化。價值正轉往其他地方：資料、嵌入式體驗、營運資金、詐欺情報，以及環繞每筆交易的軟體。移轉資金只是基本門檻，真正的利潤存在於更上層的服務。了解核心處理服務同質化時，支付價值究竟在哪裡創造、領先業者如何在交易之外將資料、軟體及嵌入式金融轉化為收入，以及如何向價值鏈上層攀升。

title: Pay It Forward
description: Whether you're a student starting out, a finance professional planning a career pivot, or a startup founder facing a specific business challenge, Pay It Forward connects you with established industry professionals for face-to-face, one-to-one mentorship. It's a chance to get advice from people who have already worked through the challenges you're facing. Sessions are 15 minutes long and take place at the Pay It Forward Lounge in Hall 3, from 18 to 20 November, 12.30pm to 4.30pm. Come with one specific question or challenge, and leave with focused, practical advice.
description_zh: 無論你是剛起步的學生、規劃職涯轉型的金融專業人士，還是面臨特定業務挑戰的新創公司創辦人，Pay It Forward 都能讓你與資深業界專業人士面對面，接受一對一指導。這是一個向已經歷並解決過你目前所面對挑戰的人請益的機會。每次諮詢為 15 分鐘，於 11 月 18 日至 20 日下午 12:30 至 4:30，在第 3 展廳的 Pay It Forward Lounge 舉行。帶著一個具體問題或挑戰前來，獲得聚焦且實用的建議。

title: Rewiring the Founder Playbook: Welcome to Founders Stage - Day 3
description: Rewiring the Founder Playbook is where founders, investors, enterprise buyers and policymakers confront the decisions reshaping the next generation of financial companies: who gets funded, what buyers will pay for, which moats survive AI, and when growth should become an exit. Flagship Founders Peak talks reveal the personal stories behind those decisions.
description_zh: Rewiring the Founder Playbook 匯聚創辦人、投資人、企業買方及政策制定者，共同直面正在重塑下一代金融公司的決策：誰能獲得資金、買方願意為什麼付費、哪些護城河能在 AI 時代存續，以及何時應將成長轉為退出。旗艦 Founders Peak 演講將揭示這些決策背後的個人故事。
