title: "What’s In It for Me?" Rewriting the Business Case for Sustainability with Green 100
description:
For all the talk about sustainability, businesses have rarely gotten a satisfying answer to one question: what's in it for me? Launched in May 2026, Singapore's Green 100 National Movement set out to change that—tying sustainability directly to tangible business value. As it accelerates towards its next milestone at the Singapore FinTech Festival, this session convenes market leaders across procurement and finance to unpack the commercial propositions forming around Green 100 Badges.

You will learn: how earning a Badge can unlock preferential procurement and supply-chain access, what financing incentives and recognition follow, and how Singapore's largest players are attaching real value to going green. This is where the business case for sustainability gets rewritten.
description_zh: 儘管永續議題受到廣泛討論，企業對一個問題卻很少得到滿意的答案：這對我有什麼好處？2026 年 5 月啟動的新加坡 Green 100 全國運動，旨在改變這個局面，將永續直接連結到具體的商業價值。隨著這項運動加速邁向新加坡金融科技節的下一個里程碑，本場次召集採購及金融領域的市場領袖，解析圍繞 Green 100 徽章逐漸形成的商業價值主張。你將了解：取得徽章如何帶來優先採購及供應鏈准入機會、隨之而來的融資誘因與認可，以及新加坡規模最大的業者如何為綠色轉型賦予實質價值。永續的商業理由將在此重新定義。

title: The Speed-Trust Paradox: Can Trust Keep Up with Agentic Finance? - Powered by MongoDB
description: As AI in finance shifts from advising to acting, institutions face a speed–trust paradox. Using MAS' Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime (SAFR) framework as a lens, this discussion explores why the data moat must evolve from volume to an operational foundation that carries trusted identity, mandate, disposition and audit data across agents, workflows and jurisdictions.
description_zh: 隨著金融領域的 AI 從提供建議轉向採取行動，機構面臨速度與信任之間的矛盾。本場討論以新加坡金融管理局（MAS）的代理型金融執行期間保障（Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime，SAFR）架構為視角，探討為何資料護城河必須從資料量優勢，演進為一套營運基礎，讓可信的身分、授權、處置及稽核資料得以跨代理、工作流程及司法管轄區流通。

title: Are Secondaries and Strategic Consolidations the Most Workable Exit Path Now?
description: Venture survival depends on cash distributions, yet public listing routes remain narrow for Southeast Asian tech firms. Bain & Company's SEA Venture Capital Report highlights that while public IPO pipelines remain stalled across domestic bourses, secondary transactions, corporate consolidations, and private equity buyouts generated over $6 billion in regional exit value. With institutional LPs demanding realized DPI over unrealized paper gains, fund managers are redesigning liquidity timelines. This session analyses how leading allocators and founders are engineering secondary sales, structured earn-outs, and strategic trade sales when public capital markets stay constrained.
description_zh: 創投能否存續取決於現金分配，但東南亞科技公司的公開上市途徑仍然狹窄。貝恩公司（Bain & Company）的東南亞創投報告指出，儘管各國交易所的 IPO 進程仍陷於停滯，次級交易、企業整併及私募股權收購，已為該區域創造超過 60 億美元的退出價值。隨著機構有限合夥人（LP）要求已實現的投入資本分配倍數（DPI），而非尚未實現的帳面收益，基金經理人正重新設計流動性時程。本場次分析在公開資本市場持續受限時，領先的資本配置者與創辦人，如何安排次級股權出售、結構化績效對價及策略性出售。

title: Stablecoins and the Future of Corporate Treasury - Powered by Mobi Asia
description: What if corporate treasury didn't need banks, borders, or business hours to move money? This session imagines a future where corporates hold, move, and grow liquidity globally on their own terms, and what it would take to get there.
description_zh: 如果企業財務管理在移轉資金時，不再需要銀行、不再受國界或營業時間限制，會是什麼樣貌？本場次構想企業依照自身條件，在全球持有、移轉並增長流動資金的未來，以及實現這個未來需要具備什麼。

title: Re: Building the Next Generation of Sustainable Real Estate
description:
Much of Asia's 2050 building stock already exists today. So the real question isn't just how to build greener—it's how far we can push the buildings we already have. The Re:Building Innovation Challenge puts that to the test, launching at the Singapore FinTech Festival as a collaborative sandbox where building owners, technology providers and built environment experts identify high-impact retrofits and model them against green building benchmarks.

You will learn: which interventions across energy, cooling and resource efficiency deliver the greatest real-world impact, where the economics still fall short, and what it takes to move from pilots to scale across Asia's existing assets. The future of green building may already be built.
description_zh: 亞洲在 2050 年仍將使用的建築，有很大一部分今天就已存在。因此，真正的問題不只是如何建得更環保，而是我們能將既有建築的表現提升到什麼程度。Re:Building Innovation Challenge 將在新加坡金融科技節啟動，以協作沙盒的形式進行驗證，讓建築業主、技術供應商及建成環境專家，共同找出高效益改造措施，並依綠建築基準進行建模評估。你將了解：能源、冷卻及資源效率領域的哪些措施能帶來最大的實際影響、哪些地方的經濟效益仍不足，以及如何在亞洲既有資產中從試點走向規模化。綠建築的未來，可能早已建成。

title: The Napkin Pitch Is Dead. What Gets an Emerging-Market Fintech Funded?
description: Capital hasn't left emerging-market fintech. It has just stopped funding the napkin. In the first half of 2026, Southeast Asian fintechs raised US$682 million and MENA fintechs raised US$617 million. In both regions a single round took a third or more of the total, and the number of deals fell sharply. Investors now want real revenue and a short road to profitability before they commit. Investors from the Gulf and North Asia sit alongside two Southeast Asian fintechs to compare what each market rewards, which metrics get a term sheet signed and what founders should ask of the investors they bring onto their cap table.
description_zh: 資本並未離開新興市場金融科技，只是不再為餐巾紙上的構想買單。2026 年上半年，東南亞金融科技公司募得 6.82 億美元，中東及北非（MENA）金融科技公司則募得 6.17 億美元。兩個區域都由單一融資輪占去總額的三分之一或更多，交易筆數也大幅下降。投資人如今要求先看到真實營收及短期內可實現獲利的路徑，才願意投入。來自海灣地區與北亞的投資人，將與兩家東南亞金融科技公司同台，比較各市場看重什麼、哪些指標能促成投資條款書簽署，以及創辦人在引入股東名冊上的投資人時，應向他們提出哪些要求。

title: Payments beyond Borders: Can Trust Transcend Geopolitical Boundaries? - Powered by NPCI
description: As geopolitics redraws trade, capital and data flows, trusted payment infrastructure is becoming a strategic priority for nations. Drawing on experiences from India and ASEAN, the session will explore how countries can build resilient, inclusive and locally governed payment foundations while staying globally connected and examine practical approaches for linking domestic payment systems across bilateral and regional payment corridors.
description_zh: 隨著地緣政治重新描繪貿易、資本及資料的流向，可信的支付基礎設施正成為各國的策略優先事項。本場次將借鏡印度及東協的經驗，探討各國如何在維持全球連結的同時，建立具韌性、包容性且由本地治理的支付基礎，並檢視透過雙邊及區域支付走廊連結國內支付系統的實務做法。

title: Beyond Compliance: Building a Holistic AI Fraud Surveillance to Combat Financial Fraud - Powered by Accenture
description: Financial crime doesn't operate in silos, yet most fraud detection tools do. Today's landscape is filled with point solutions: KYC platforms that stop at onboarding, AML engines focused on transaction monitoring, and network graph tools that excel technically. Fraud signals are everywhere, but data remains fragmented. AI Fraud Surveillance unifies financial, qualitative, and network signals into a single view, enabling fraud detection before it happens, not after.
description_zh: 金融犯罪不會各自孤立地運作，但多數詐欺偵測工具卻是如此。今日市場充斥著單點解決方案：僅處理客戶開戶的 KYC 平台、聚焦交易監控的洗錢防制引擎，以及技術表現出色的網路關係圖工具。詐欺訊號無所不在，資料卻仍然零散。AI Fraud Surveillance 將財務、質性及網路訊號整合成單一視圖，讓詐欺得以在發生之前被偵測，而不是事後才發現。

title: Scaling Green Digital Infrastructure: A Regional Policy Dialogue
description:
As sustainability requirements expand across Asia, trusted sustainability data—collected, exchanged and acted on across value chains—is fast becoming critical economic infrastructure. Early moves by regulators, central banks and development institutions already hint at how shared digital platforms can power sustainability reporting, enable green finance and unlock new commercial value. This regional policy dialogue convenes the Monetary Authority of Singapore, the Bank of Thailand, the Securities and Exchange Commission Philippines, and the Asian Development Bank to ask what a national digital infrastructure for sustainability looks like.

You will learn: where green digital infrastructure creates the greatest value, what it takes to move from early initiatives to broad adoption, and how public leadership and private innovation can build the foundations for Asia's transition.
description_zh: 隨著永續要求在亞洲持續擴展，跨價值鏈蒐集、交換並據以行動的可信永續資料，正迅速成為關鍵經濟基礎設施。監管機關、中央銀行及開發機構的早期行動，已展現共用數位平台如何支持永續報告、促進綠色金融並創造新的商業價值。本場區域政策對話邀集新加坡金融管理局、泰國央行、菲律賓證券交易委員會及亞洲開發銀行，共同探討國家級永續數位基礎設施應有什麼樣貌。你將了解：綠色數位基礎設施在哪裡創造最大價值、從早期計畫走向廣泛採用需要哪些條件，以及公部門領導與民間創新如何為亞洲轉型奠定基礎。

title: The South–South Playbook: Rewiring Finance for the Remaining 1.6 Billion Unbanked
speakers: Hélder Lopes; Dr. Patrick Njoroge; Nasim Aliev; Irene Arias Hofman
description: Emerging markets have built some of the world’s most innovative models for financial inclusion. This panel explores what Africa and Asia can learn directly from each other — from digital public infrastructure and payments to regulation and public-private partnerships — and whether a new South–South playbook can accelerate the next phase of financial inclusion.
description_zh: 新興市場已建立一些全球最具創新性的普惠金融模式。本場論壇探討非洲與亞洲可以直接向彼此學習什麼，範圍涵蓋數位公共基礎設施、支付、監管及公私協力合作，以及一套新的南南合作行動方針，能否加速普惠金融的下一階段發展。

title: The Future of Trust: Deepfakes, Synthetic Identity and Proof in the Age of Generative AI
speakers: Aishwarya Jayakumar; Iain Armstrong; Minh Nguyen; Yair Tal; Josef Jelinek
description:
In a world of synthetic everything, proof is becoming the scarcest commodity in finance. As AI-generated identities, deepfakes, and convincing digital deception become routine, institutions can no longer assume authenticity; they have to verify it. This session frames the problem and then works through the answer.

It opens with the shift underneath the shift: once trust can no longer be assumed, the burden moves from catching fakes after the fact to proving authenticity before a transaction happens at all. That reframes what needs to be provable rather than assumed, and who is positioned to build the systems that prove it. The discussion then gets specific about the different bets being placed on how to solve this: catching synthetic fraud at the point of verification, proving identity cryptographically without exposing the underlying data at all, and building the credential infrastructure that ties it together.

Attendees hear where each approach actually holds up against a motivated forger, and where the gaps between them still leave room for one to slip through.
description_zh: 在萬物皆可合成的世界中，證明正成為金融領域最稀缺的資源。隨著 AI 生成身分、深偽技術及足以亂真的數位欺騙變得常見，機構已無法假定事物真實，而必須加以驗證。本場次先界定問題，再逐步探索答案。首先探討變革背後更深一層的轉變：一旦信任不再能被視為理所當然，責任重點便從事後抓出偽造，轉向在交易發生之前就證明真實性。這重新界定了哪些事項必須能被證明、而不能只是預設成立，以及誰有條件建造提供這些證明的系統。接著，討論將具體檢視不同的解題途徑：在驗證環節攔截合成詐欺、在完全不暴露底層資料的情況下以密碼學證明身分，以及建構將各環節串接起來的憑證基礎設施。與會者將聽到各種方法在哪些情況下確實能抵擋蓄意偽造者，以及方法之間的哪些缺口仍可能讓偽造者趁隙而入。

title: Can An AI Wrapper Ever Become a Scalable Business?
description: Adding conversational wrappers and light automation layers over third-party models provided quick early ARR, but enterprise buyers are cutting through the veneer. Carta’s State of Private Markets analysis reveals that software companies driven by signed enterprise workflow contracts trade at a median 11.8x revenue, whereas startups reliant on pilot or usage-based AI features clear at just 5.2x. Furthermore, McKinsey’s enterprise AI research highlights that fewer than 20% of adopting companies report bottom-line EBIT impact. This session equips founders to construct defensible domain data integrations and proprietary workflows that survive upstream platform commoditization.
description_zh: 在第三方模型上加上對話式介面及輕量自動化層，曾快速帶來早期年度經常性收入（ARR），但企業買方正逐漸看穿這層包裝。Carta 的《私募市場現況》分析顯示，以已簽署的企業工作流程合約驅動業務的軟體公司，其交易估值營收倍數中位數為 11.8 倍；依賴試點或按使用量計費 AI 功能的新創公司，則僅為 5.2 倍。此外，麥肯錫的企業 AI 研究指出，採用 AI 的公司中，不到 20% 回報息稅前利潤（EBIT）受到實質影響。本場次將協助創辦人建立具有競爭防禦力的領域資料整合與專有工作流程，使企業能在上游平台同質化的過程中存續。

title: C:\>DIR Agentic Regulator Showcase
description:
AI agents are already executing workflows and making decisions at machine speed across financial systems and digital markets. Supervisors are being asked to oversee them with tools built for a slower world.

The Cambridge Digital Innovation and Regulation Initiative (C:\>DIR), hosted by Financial Innovation for Impact launched the Global 'Agentic Regulator' Hackathon in September this year.

The hackathon brought together multidisciplinary teams from the public and private sectors to work on that gap, building explainable, deployable prototypes across six priority areas:

- Agentic Financial and High Stakes AI Advice (supported by Moneybox)

- Agentic Payments, Commerce & their Oversight (supported by Ant International)

- Decentralised Market Infrastructure, Smart Contracts & AI Agents (supported by the Ethereum Foundation)

- AI-Driven Fraud and Scams

- Know Your Agent (KY-A), Digital Verification and Digital Public Infrastructure

- Market Manipulation, Agentic Herding & Stability

The winning teams now bring their work to the Catalyst Stage at the Singapore FinTech Festival. Come and see what the future of supervision could look like.
description_zh: AI 代理已在金融系統及數位市場中，以機器速度執行工作流程並做出決策。監理者卻被要求使用為較慢節奏世界打造的工具來監督它們。由 Financial Innovation for Impact 承辦的 Cambridge Digital Innovation and Regulation Initiative（C:\>DIR），於今年 9 月推出全球「Agentic Regulator」黑客松。活動匯聚公私部門的跨領域團隊，針對這項落差，在六個優先領域建構可解釋、可部署的原型：代理型金融與高風險 AI 諮詢（由 Moneybox 支持）；代理型支付、商業及其監督（由 Ant International 支持）；去中心化市場基礎設施、智慧合約與 AI 代理（由 Ethereum Foundation 支持）；AI 驅動的詐欺與詐騙；認識你的代理（KY-A）、數位驗證及數位公共基礎設施；市場操縱、代理群聚行為與穩定性。獲勝團隊現在將把成果帶到新加坡金融科技節的 Catalyst Stage。一起來看看監理的未來可能是什麼樣貌。

title: Anchoring Digital Financial Markets
description:
Tokenisation has moved well past the pilot stage, but a market only works if the infrastructure underneath it can be trusted: networks built for institutional scale, platforms that connect issuance, trading and settlement, a trusted form of money to settle in, and an infrastructure that lets institutions run digital assets as everyday business. This panel brings together the people building each of those layers.

The discussion works through what each layer needs to hold up under real institutional volumes, where the handoffs between networks, platforms, settlement money and legacy systems still cause friction, and what the operating model behind digital assets looks like in practice: who runs what, how it connects to existing infrastructure, and what it takes to scale. Attendees leave with a practical view of what "anchoring" digital markets means, from the network to the money that settles on it.
description_zh: 代幣化早已跨越試點階段，但市場要能運作，底層基礎設施就必須值得信賴：為機構規模打造的網路、連結發行、交易及結算的平台、可信賴的結算貨幣，以及讓機構能將數位資產作為日常業務運作的基礎設施。本場論壇匯聚建構各個層次的實務工作者。討論將逐一探討每個層次需要什麼才能承受真實的機構交易量、網路、平台、結算貨幣及傳統系統之間的銜接在哪裡仍造成阻力，以及數位資產背後的營運模式實際是什麼樣貌：誰負責什麼、如何連接既有基礎設施，以及擴大規模需要哪些條件。與會者將從網路到其上用於結算的貨幣，務實了解為數位市場「奠定穩固基礎」的含義。

title: From Invisible to Investable: Building the Financial Infrastructure for the Next Billion
speakers: Allen Forlemu; Miller Abel; Munir Duri; Francesca Aliverti
description: Billions of people and small businesses remain outside formal credit because financial institutions cannot reliably identify, assess or price their risk. This panel examines how payment infrastructure, digital identity, transaction data and AI can change that — turning previously invisible economic activity into a basis for lending and investment.
description_zh: 數十億人口及小型企業仍無法取得正規信貸，因為金融機構無法可靠地辨識、評估其風險或為風險定價。本場論壇探討支付基礎設施、數位身分、交易資料及 AI 如何改變這種情況，將過去不可見的經濟活動轉化為放款與投資的依據。

title: From Data Chaos to AI-Ready: The Agent Behind Every Insurance Advisor - Powered by Microsoft
description: AI's real blocker isn't the model, it's unstructured data. This live demo shows an agent that scans external market signals, matches them to an advisor's book, and turns a headline into a qualified proposal, so advisors arrive don't just walk in prepared, they proactively create the next opportunity. See Microsoft's Work IQ, Foundry IQ, Fabric IQ and Web IQ orchestrating as one platform to make this a reality.
description_zh: AI 真正的阻礙不是模型，而是非結構化資料。本次現場示範將展示一個代理，掃描外部市場訊號、與顧問的客戶組合配對，並將一則新聞標題轉化為經篩選的合適提案，讓顧問不只是有備而來，更能主動創造下一個機會。看看 Microsoft 的 Work IQ、Foundry IQ、Fabric IQ 及 Web IQ 如何整合協作成單一平台，讓這一切成真。

title: Beyond Credit Scoring: AI in Risk Modelling, Strategy and Oversight - Powered by CloudunAI
description: How is AI changing the work behind credit decisions? Drawing on cases from Southeast Asia and Latin America, this session explores AI execution and AI-assisted oversight across feature engineering, modelling and credit strategy. Attendees will see a practical workflow, its evaluation results, and where human judgement remains essential.
description_zh: AI 正如何改變信貸決策背後的工作？本場次借鏡東南亞及拉丁美洲的案例，探討特徵工程、建模及信貸策略中的 AI 執行與 AI 輔助監督。與會者將看到實際工作流程、評估結果，以及哪些環節仍不可或缺地需要人類判斷。

title: Can Europe and Asia Build the Next Global Wealth Corridor?
speakers: James Verner; Lavanya Chari; Prof. R. Alexander Lorz; Alex Panican; Nishtha Asthana
description: Europe and Asia have capital, investment products and increasingly global investors, but the infrastructure connecting them remains fragmented. Different regulations, fund structures, data standards and distribution systems continue to limit access and raise costs. This session examines what it would take to create a trusted wealth corridor between the regions, from regulatory interoperability and digital fund distribution to common data and identity rails. It asks how governments, financial centres, asset managers, banks and fintech platforms can reduce friction without weakening investor protection.
description_zh: 歐洲與亞洲擁有資本、投資產品，以及日益全球化的投資人，但連結兩地的基礎設施仍然零散。不同的法規、基金結構、資料標準及分銷系統，持續限制市場接入並推高成本。本場次探討建立兩地之間可信財富走廊所需的條件，範圍從監管互通、數位基金分銷，到共通資料及身分基礎通道。討論將檢視政府、金融中心、資產管理業者、銀行及金融科技平台，如何在不削弱投資人保護的前提下減少阻力。

title: Skills Gaps and the Shape of Tomorrow's Financial Institutions
speakers: Mostapha Tahiri; Osamu Abe; Akanksha Rath
description: Talent rewiring is redrawing the map itself, institutions now follow people first, capital and headquarters second. Financial institutions increasingly decide where to build based on where the talent already is, not just where capital or headquarters sit. This discussion looks at how that dynamic is redrawing where banks locate technology and operations, and what it means for markets competing to become talent hubs rather than just financial centres. The key question it looks to answer: is tomorrow's bank shaped more by where the talent is than by where the capital is?
description_zh: 人才重塑正在重畫版圖本身——機構如今先跟著人走，資本與總部反而其次。金融機構愈來愈依據「人才已經在哪裡」來決定在哪裡設點，而不只看資本或總部落在何處。本場討論探討這股動力如何重新劃定銀行的技術與營運據點，以及這對那些競相成為人才樞紐、而不只是金融中心的市場意味著什麼。它想回答的關鍵問題是：未來的銀行，是由人才在哪裡、而非資本在哪裡形塑的嗎？

title: What Operating Habits Must Founders Abandon to Stay Fundable?
description: The boom-era playbook of subsidizing unprofitable top-line expansion with venture equity now leads directly to insolvency. Industry data from Bessemer Venture Partners shows the benchmark efficiency metric—net new ARR divided by net burn—has shifted from a tolerable 0.5x in 2021 to a mandatory 1.5x+ for top-quartile financings today. Investors are actively penalizing management teams that burn cash on vanity marketing campaigns and premature geographic expansion. This session brings institutional venture allocators to detail the exact operating controls founders must implement immediately, alongside the growth habits they must permanently eliminate.
description_zh: 繁榮時期以創投股權資金補貼無利可圖的營收擴張，這套做法如今會直接導致無力償債。Bessemer Venture Partners 的產業數據顯示，作為基準的效率指標，即淨新增年度經常性收入（ARR）除以淨現金消耗，已從 2021 年尚可接受的 0.5 倍，轉為如今排名前四分之一融資案必須達到的 1.5 倍以上。投資人正積極懲罰將現金耗費於虛榮式行銷活動及過早地域擴張的管理團隊。本場次邀請機構創投資本配置者，詳細說明創辦人必須立即落實的具體營運控管，以及必須永久摒棄的成長習慣。

title: The Missing Middle: Powering the Next Wave of Commercial Payment Corridors
description: While most payments conversations focus on consumer rails, the real bottleneck may be commercial: B2B and merchant payments across Asia, the Middle East and Africa remain fragmented and cash-heavy. This panel unpacks what it takes to build commercial payment corridors that actually work and where the friction still lies.
description_zh: 多數支付討論聚焦消費者支付通道，但真正的瓶頸可能在商業支付：亞洲、中東及非洲的企業對企業（B2B）與商家支付仍然零散，並高度依賴現金。本場論壇解析打造真正有效的商業支付走廊需要具備什麼，以及阻力仍存在於哪些環節。

title: Asia's Payments Moment: Building Connectivity Across ASEAN and Beyond
description:
Bilateral links between Asia's national instant-payment systems already exist and are multiplying. QR code interoperability between several member states has been live for years, built one country pair at a time. The next opportunity is a genuinely connected system, one where a payment initiated in any linked market settles instantly in any other, without each pair of countries negotiating its own bridge. As Singapore prepares to take over the ASEAN chairmanship from the Philippines in 2027, regional payment connectivity is shaping up to be one of the flagship items on its agenda, and this session is where that opportunity gets mapped out, a year ahead of time.

This panel brings together central bank representatives from across ASEAN and India to discuss what a genuinely connected instant-payment system could unlock: aligning local-currency settlement frameworks, building on the links already in place, from ASEAN's QR interoperability to the UPI-PayNow corridor, to reach true multilateral interoperability, and establishing the shared governance that lets partners trust a system built together rather than one at a time. Attendees leave with a clear view of the progress already made, what Singapore's incoming ASEAN chairmanship could prioritise, and how close the wider region actually is to instant payments that work the same way whether you're paying across the street or across a border.
description_zh: 亞洲各國即時支付系統之間的雙邊連結已經存在，且正不斷增加。數個成員國之間的 QR 碼互通已運作多年，都是逐一按國家配對建立。下一個機會是打造真正連通的系統，讓在任何已連結市場發起的付款，都能在另一個市場即時結算，不必由每一對國家各自協商連接方式。隨著新加坡準備於 2027 年接替菲律賓擔任東協輪值主席，區域支付互聯正逐漸成為其議程中的旗艦項目之一，本場次將提前一年勾勒這項機會。本場論壇匯聚東協各國及印度的央行代表，討論真正連通的即時支付系統能釋放哪些可能：對接本幣結算架構、以既有連結為基礎，從東協 QR 碼互通到 UPI-PayNow 走廊，實現真正的多邊互通，並建立共同治理，讓夥伴信任共同打造的系統，而非逐一各自建立的連結。與會者將清楚了解已取得的進展、新加坡即將接任東協主席時可能優先推動的事項，以及整個區域距離這樣的即時支付還有多遠：無論付款給街道對面的對象，還是跨境付款，都能以相同方式運作。

title: Criminals Deployed Agents First. Can Real-Time Controls Catch Up?
description: Fraudsters didn't wait for a governance framework. Autonomous agents are already probing payment rails, spinning up synthetic identities and running social-engineering scripts at machine speed, while many institutions still triage alerts in batches. With instant payments and agentic commerce scaling fast, the window between attack and response is now measured in milliseconds. The panel looks at where real-time controls are keeping pace and where they are structurally behind. It also covers how to tell a legitimate customer's agent from a malicious one, and what defending with agents looks like when regulators still expect a human in the loop.
description_zh: 詐欺者並沒有等待治理架構到位。自主代理早已開始探測支付通道、建立合成身分，並以機器速度執行社交工程腳本，許多機構卻仍然以批次方式分流處理警報。隨著即時支付及代理型商業快速擴張，從攻擊到回應的時間窗口如今已以毫秒計算。本場論壇探討即時控管在哪些地方跟得上，又在哪些地方結構性落後。也將討論如何區分合法客戶的代理與惡意代理，以及當監管機關仍要求人類介入時，運用代理防禦會是什麼樣貌。

title: The Uneven Map: Where AI Rewrites Commerce First
speakers: Eun Mi Kristina Rhee; Tang Wei
description:
The protocol race is over faster than anyone expected. Visa, Google, Mastercard, OpenAI, Stripe and Ant International have all shipped agent-initiated payment infrastructure, while countries such as Korea alone recorded over 100 million AI-to-AI payments in seven months. This discussion will be around where machine will transact first, at what granularity, and on whose stack.

That question does not have a global answer, because agentic commerce is gated by four preconditions that are unevenly distributed or agreed upon.

Identity: can an agent be issued a provable, scoped, revocable mandate.

Acceptance density: is there enough merchant coverage for an agent's choice to be meaningful.

Settlement granularity: can value move at machine speed and sub-cent size.

Customer trust and value: will people actually delegate? Does the result make everyday finance simpler, more transparent and more accessible, including for customers that conventional banking has overlooked?

The first three are being solved on the rails; the fourth is decided in the customer relationship. This panel puts both views on one stage: the platforms building agentic infrastructure, and a digital bank that rebuilt banking around customer needs. Together they map the next eighteen months by looking look at where AI creates practical customer value first and how institutions should balance automation with human judgment and accountability.
description_zh: 協定競賽結束得比任何人預期都快。Visa、Google、Mastercard、OpenAI、Stripe 及 Ant International 都已推出由代理發起的支付基礎設施；在部分國家中，光是韓國就在七個月內記錄了逾 1 億筆 AI 對 AI 支付。本場討論將圍繞機器會先在哪裡交易、以多細的粒度交易，以及使用誰的技術架構展開。這個問題沒有全球通用的答案，因為代理型商業受四項前提限制，而它們的分布或共識並不均衡。身分：能否向代理核發可驗證、範圍明確且可撤銷的授權。受理密度：商家覆蓋是否足夠，讓代理的選擇具有意義。結算粒度：價值能否以機器速度、低於一分的金額移轉。客戶信任與價值：人們真的會委託代理嗎？結果是否讓日常金融變得更簡單、透明且容易取得，包括對傳統銀行業忽略的客戶而言？前三項正透過底層通道解決，第四項則取決於客戶關係。本場論壇將兩種觀點帶到同一舞台：建構代理型基礎設施的平台，以及一家圍繞客戶需求重新打造銀行服務的數位銀行。他們將共同勾勒未來十八個月的發展，探討 AI 會先在哪些地方為客戶創造實際價值，以及機構應如何平衡自動化、人類判斷與問責。

title: Reskilling the Workforce: What's the Right Split Between Employers, Universities, Governments and Multilaterals?
How to Protect Founder Equity Through Funding Challenges in 2027?
description: Cheap venture funding has evaporated, leaving founders facing demanding structural terms. According to PitchBook deal terms data, over 25% of late-stage financings have priced flat or down, while Cooley's Venture Financing Report recorded liquidation preference multiples above 1.0x climbing to 22% in growth rounds. Investors holding dry powder are enforcing aggressive participating preferences, redemption schedules, and board vetoes that strip founder control. For leadership teams navigating single-digit runway, survival requires understanding which covenants preserve long-term agency and which turn founders into salaried operators on their own cap tables.
description_zh: 低成本創投資金已經消失，創辦人因此面臨苛刻的交易結構條款。根據 PitchBook 的交易條款數據，超過 25% 的後期融資估值持平或下降；Cooley 的《創業融資報告》則記錄，成長期融資中清算優先權倍數高於 1.0 倍的占比攀升至 22%。持有待投資金的投資人，正強勢要求參與型優先權、贖回時程及董事會否決權，剝奪創辦人的控制權。對於資金續航只剩個位數月份的領導團隊，生存的關鍵在於了解：哪些契約條款能保留長期自主權，哪些則會讓創辦人在自己的股權結構中，淪為領薪的營運者。

title: The Next Alpha of the Payment Value Chain
speakers: Manoj Dugar; Michael Gao; Yang Wenhui
description: Payments are becoming faster and cheaper, but where will the industry make money next? This panel looks at where new revenue pools are emerging across the payments value chain — from data and embedded services to cross-border flows and new forms of money — and which business models can capture them from 2027 onwards.
description_zh: 支付正變得更快速、更便宜，但這個產業下一步將從哪裡獲利？本場論壇探討支付價值鏈中正在出現的新營收來源，從資料、嵌入式服務，到跨境資金流及新型態貨幣，並檢視哪些商業模式能從 2027 年起掌握這些機會。
